title: Require machine-readable ops review verdict and fail closed on process errors
description: Ops review output currently accepts standalone APPROVED/REJECTED and parseResult can return approved/rejected even when the subprocess exits nonzero. The review gate must require a machine-readable terminal verdict contract (VERDICT: APPROVED or VERDICT: REJECTED) and approval must require verdict approved plus process success plus no timeout/error. Bare textual APPROVED inside stdout is never sufficient by itself.

title: Make oro work fail closed when ops review cannot approve
description: cmd/oro/cmd_work.go reviewLoop currently treats failed or unknown ops review verdicts as non-blocking and logs "continuing without review". That conflicts with the dispatcher standard: review execution errors, timeouts, failed verdicts, and unknown verdicts must not be treated as approval. oro work should stop, return an error, or leave the bead/branch unmerged with an explicit blocked/incomplete state rather than proceeding as though review was optional.

title: P0: TestCLIBeadSource_UpdateInProgressPersists fails — bd auto-export warning corrupts JSON output
description:
## Symptom
QG `go test ./pkg/dispatcher/...` fails on `TestCLIBeadSource_UpdateInProgressPersists`:
```
beadsource_test.go:1940: parse bd create output: invalid character 'W' after top-level value
output: {
  "id": "bd_001-7pd",
  ...
}
Warning: auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1
```

## Root Cause
- `bd 1.0.2` writes "Warning: auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1" to stdout/stderr after every command when its internal git add fails.
- Inside the test's tmpDir, .beads/issues.jsonl is gitignored (per 2026-04-27 decision: JSONL sync broke too often, Dolt is source of truth) so `git add .beads/issues.jsonl` fails.
- The test uses `cmd.CombinedOutput()` (beadsource_test.go:1920) which mixes stdout+stderr, so the warning appears in the buffer the test passes to `json.Unmarshal`.
- Test was added 2026-04-20 (commit 83e7891a) before the gitignore decision today (2026-04-27).

## Reproduction
`go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestCLIBeadSource_UpdateInProgressPersists -count=1` from any worktree on the repo. Deterministic.

## Suggested Fix
1. Prefer: switch test from `CombinedOutput()` to `Output()` and only parse stdout. Verify bd writes JSON to stdout and warnings to stderr.
2. Alternative: filter the warning line out of CombinedOutput before json.Unmarshal.
3. Alternative: pass `--quiet` to `bd create` in the test (suppresses non-essential output).

## Discovered While
Completing oro-psng (pkg/protocol architect→manager comment+fixture cleanup). My changes only modified pkg/protocol/schema.go (4 lines) and pkg/protocol/schema_test.go (6 lines) and cannot affect pkg/dispatcher tests; QG fails on this unrelated dispatcher test.

## Files
- pkg/dispatcher/beadsource_test.go:1907 (test fn)
- pkg/dispatcher/beadsource_test.go:1920 (cmd.CombinedOutput call)
- pkg/dispatcher/beadsource_test.go:1933 (bd create invocation)
- pkg/dispatcher/beadsource_test.go:1940 (json.Unmarshal that fails)
acceptance_criteria: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestCLIBeadSource_UpdateInProgressPersists -count=1 -timeout 60s passes
close_reason: Fixed: switched CombinedOutput() to Output() in test run helper to isolate bd stderr warnings; added waitFor polling for bead_requeued_scale_down event check. Both dispatcher tests pass.

title: [epic] Make ops review process timeout configurable via --review-timeout
description: Two ops reviews timed out at hardcoded 10m on 2026-04-27 (oro-l8yv 04:52:27, oro-ane4 04:58:31), causing manager STUCK_WORKER escalations and zero merges this session. Root cause: pkg/ops/ops.go:81 hardcodes OpsReview timeout at 10m, bypassing the --review-timeout CLI flag (which only feeds Dispatcher.ReviewTimeout, the worker-stall escalation timer at dispatcher.go:362). title: Fix stage_assets_test.go cleanup destroying _assets for subsequent CI steps
description:
## Bug

`TestStageAssetsUsesRepoAssetsDir` in `cmd/oro/stage_assets_test.go` (line 64) calls `os.RemoveAll(assetsDir)` as cleanup, which deletes `cmd/oro/_assets/`. This causes the CI "Build" step (`go build ./...`) to fail with:

```
cmd/oro/embed.go:9:12: pattern all:_assets: no matching files found
```

**Root cause**: The test deletes `_assets/` at the end (line 64), but `go build ./...` runs AFTER `go test` in CI and needs `_assets/` to compile `embed.go`.

**Timeline in CI**:
1. `make stage-assets` creates `_assets/` (step 4)
2. `go test -race ./cmd/...` compiles cmd/oro (embed works) (step 10)
3. During test execution, `TestStageAssetsUsesRepoAssetsDir` deletes `_assets/`, re-stages via `make stage-assets`, then deletes AGAIN at cleanup (line 64)
4. `go build ./...` runs → `_assets/` gone → FAIL (step 12)

## Fix

In `cmd/oro/stage_assets_test.go`, replace the cleanup `os.RemoveAll` at line 64 with a `t.Cleanup` that re-runs `make stage-assets` to restore the directory. This way the test validates stage-assets behavior without destroying shared build state.

Alternatively, the simpler fix: just remove the cleanup entirely (lines 63-66). The CI workflow already runs `make clean-assets` at the end (step 14, `if: always()`), and locally `make test` also calls `clean-assets` after testing. The test does not need to clean up after itself.

**Preferred approach**: Remove lines 63-66 (the cleanup block). The `_assets/` directory is already `.gitignore`d and cleaned up by the Makefile targets.

Also remove lines 17-20 (the pre-clean). The test should work regardless of whether `_assets/` exists before it runs — the `make stage-assets` call is idempotent.

## Files
- `cmd/oro/stage_assets_test.go` — Remove cleanup (lines 63-66) and pre-clean (lines 17-20)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `go test ./cmd/oro/... -run TestStageAssetsUsesRepoAssetsDir -v -count=1` passes
2. After the test runs, `cmd/oro/_assets/` still exists (not deleted by cleanup)
3. `go build ./cmd/oro` succeeds after `go test ./cmd/oro/...` (no embed error)
4. CI Go job passes end-to-end (stage-assets → test → build)

title: Escalation retry loop replays stale WORKER_CRASH alerts with empty beadID
description:

1. shouldRetryEscalation returns true for WORKER_CRASH escalations with empty beadID (line 3115), causing 2675 stale escalations to be replayed every 2 minutes.

title: Runaway worker spawning in daemon mode (66 idle workers)
description: When running dispatcher in daemon-only mode with scale directive, observed 66 idle workers despite target=3 and MaxWorkers=2. The 2*target cap in reconcileScale should prevent this. Root cause investigation in progress: (1) applyScaleDirective sets targetWorkers but not cfg.MaxWorkers (2) reconcileScale has 2*target cap which should limit to 6 not 66 (3) Hypothesis: spawn-crash-respawn loop where workers fail to connect, get reaped, managedCount drops, more spawn. Need to check if targetWorkers gets bumped by auto_scale or repeated scale directives. Files: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go (maybeAutoScale line 2758, reconcileScale line 2795, applyScaleDirective line 2538, scaleUp line 2840). Test: verify 2*target cap holds under rapid worker churn.
notes:
Root cause confirmed: Two bugs identified.

BUG 1 (primary, explains 66 workers): The 2*target cap in reconcileScale uses totalWorkers = len(d.workers) + len(d.pendingManagedIDs), which includes UNMANAGED external workers. When 66 orphaned workers from a previous session reconnect as unmanaged, totalWorkers=66 >= 2*3=6, cap fires, and NO managed workers get spawned. User sees 66 idle unmanaged workers with 0 managed workers despite target=3.

BUG 2 (rapid churn bypass): When managed workers cycle through spawn→connect→crash→heartbeat-remove faster than reconcileScale accumulates, each call sees totalWorkers=0 and spawns target more workers. The cap never fires because totalWorkers never reaches 2*target at the moment of the check.

FIX: 
1. Add unexpectedManagedExits int field to Dispatcher
2. In checkHeartbeats: capture w.managed in deadInfo, increment d.unexpectedManagedExits for each dead managed worker
3. In reconcileScale: change cap check from 'totalWorkers >= 2*target' to 'managedCount + d.unexpectedManagedExits >= 2*target'. This (a) excludes unmanaged workers from cap, (b) accumulates crash history across cycles to prevent rapid churn bypass
4. In applyScaleDirective: reset d.unexpectedManagedExits = 0 on target change (fresh budget)
5. Remove totalWorkers variable (only used for old cap)

Test to write: TestReconcileScale_CapHoldsUnderRapidChurn
- target=3, simulate 3 cycles of spawn→connect→crash(via simulated heartbeat removal)→reconcileScale
- Assert total spawned <= 2*target=6 after all cycles

Existing test to update: TestReconcileScale_CapsAtDoubleTarget 'blocks spawn when total workers at 2x target'
- Currently uses 8 unmanaged workers to hit cap (which was the bug)
- After fix, unmanaged workers won't trigger cap; use unexpectedManagedExits instead

Files to change:
- pkg/dispatcher/worker_pool.go: checkHeartbeats - add managed field to deadInfo, increment counter
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go: add field, change cap logic in reconcileScale, reset in applyScaleDirective
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_autoscale_test.go: update existing test, add new churn test

title: Fix: scale-down silently loses in-flight beads
description:
When the dispatcher scales down and shuts down a busy worker, the bead assigned to that worker is silently lost. Both handleShutdownApproved (dispatcher.go:1594-1612) and handleShutdownTimeout (worker_pool.go:354-364) clear w.beadID without requeuing the bead or calling clearBeadTracking(). The bead stays in_progress in the beads DB forever and tracking maps leak.

Fix requires:
1. Capture beadID before clearing w.beadID in both handleShutdownTimeout() and handleShutdownApproved()
2. Call clearBeadTracking(beadID) to clean up tracking maps
3. Requeue the bead (set status back to open) so it can be reassigned
4. Log an escalation event for observability
5. Add tests: TestScaleDown_BusyWorker_BeadRequeued covering both the approved and timeout paths
acceptance_criteria:
1. handleShutdownApproved captures beadID before clearing w.beadID and calls clearBeadTracking(beadID) + requeues bead to open status
2. handleShutdownTimeout captures beadID before clearing w.beadID and calls clearBeadTracking(beadID) + requeues bead to open status
3. Requeued bead appears in bd ready output after scale-down completes
4. No tracking map leaks: inFlightBeads and beadWorker maps do not retain entries for the requeued bead
5. TestScaleDown_BusyWorker_BeadRequeued passes covering both approved and timeout shutdown paths
6. An escalation/log event is emitted when a bead is requeued due to scale-down
notes: Worker worker-1771828763652173000-1 stalled with no progress (no commits, clean worktree at .worktrees/oro-j8h8). Worker process was dead. title: Add per-type pre-check guard to escalation retry loop
description:
retryPendingEscalations (dispatcher.go:2448) blindly re-fires all pending escalations every 2 minutes without checking if the underlying condition still holds. It SELECTs only id, message — doesnt read the type or bead_id columns that are already stored in the escalations table. This causes infinite escalation spam for conditions already resolved (MISSING_AC after AC is added, STUCK_WORKER after worker is gone, MERGE_CONFLICT after branch merged).

This supersedes oro-etbo (MISSING_AC-only fix) by implementing the guard for ALL escalation types.

Fix: (1) Change SELECT to include type, bead_id. (2) Add shouldRetryEscalation(ctx, escType, beadID) method with per-type guards. (3) If condition resolved, auto-ack the escalation row (UPDATE escalations SET status=acked WHERE id=?) instead of re-sending.

Per-type guards:
- MISSING_AC: beads.Show -> AC populated -> auto-ack
- STUCK_WORKER: worker not in d.workers -> auto-ack
- WORKER_CRASH: bead not in_progress (re-queued or closed) -> auto-ack
- STUCK: bead status changed from in_progress -> auto-ack
- MERGE_CONFLICT: bead closed -> auto-ack
- PRIORITY_CONTENTION: bead is in_progress (picked up) -> auto-ack

title: Check bead status in assignBead before claiming assignment
description:
assignBead (dispatcher.go:1693) calls checkBeadReady which calls lookupBeadDetail (bd show). The bd show response returns BeadDetail (protocol/types.go:31) but BeadDetail has no Status field. assignBead trusts the bd ready snapshot from tryAssign, but there is a race window where the bead can be closed externally between bd ready and the assignBead call. This is the oro-yoov pattern: bead cherry-picked to main and marked CLOSED, but dispatcher proceeds with stale snapshot and assigns worker to a closed bead.

Fix: (1) Add Status field to protocol.BeadDetail struct. (2) Populate Status in CLIBeadSource.Show from bd show --json output. (3) In checkBeadReady, after lookupBeadDetail returns, check if status is closed — if so, log bead_closed_before_assign event and return ok=false. This gives assignBead a fresh status check using the bd show call already being made.

title: Prune bead tracking maps on worker connection close
description:
handleConn deferred cleanup (dispatcher.go:513-520) calls delete(d.workers, workerID) but never calls clearBeadTracking(beadID). When a worker process dies and its TCP connection drops, the scanner EOF triggers the deferred cleanup, removing the worker from d.workers. But BeadTracker maps (attemptCounts, qgStuckTracker, escalatedBeads, etc.) retain stale entries. Since the worker is already gone from d.workers, checkHeartbeats never sees it, so clearBeadTracking never fires for the connection-drop path. The hourly pruneStaleTracking safety net is too slow — stale qgStuckTracker entries cause false STUCK detections and stale escalatedBeads entries suppress legitimate escalations.

Fix: In handleConn's deferred cleanup, before calling delete(d.workers, workerID), capture w.beadID. After deleting, if beadID \!= empty, call clearBeadTracking(beadID).

title: Add content verification to isBranchMerged guard
description:
merge.go:164-181 isBranchMerged checks rev-list --count main..<branch>. When count is 0, it returns true with main HEAD as the merge SHA. Fix: After confirming count is 0, run `git diff main..<branch>`. If diff output is non-empty, the branch has content not on main — return false (not merged). If diff is empty, truly merged. On git diff error, return false (fail-open: proceed to rebase).

Root cause: Assignment logic doesn't check bead.status or bead.owner before assigning.

title: Fix merge pipeline: workers close beads before code lands on main
description:
## Problem
Workers mark beads as closed in their worktrees, but the merge-to-main step fails silently or never executes. Worktree cleanup then destroys the evidence (branch, commits). The bead shows "closed" with a commit hash that exists nowhere.

Audit of 2026-02-16 found **9 beads** falsely closed — code never reached main:
- oro-w451: fix on branch agent/oro-w451, never cherry-picked
- oro-vi0h: zero code exists anywhere (no branch, no commit)
- oro-ldbd, oro-z5oc.2, oro-tapy, oro-ycjj.4: claimed commits exist nowhere
- oro-p3wd, oro-9fme, oro-wm6x: no matching code patterns on main

## Root Cause Analysis

The merge flow is: worker completes → QG passes → mergeAndComplete() → cherry-pick to main → bd close → worktree cleanup.

Failure modes (all observed):
1. **Cherry-pick fails silently** — merge conflict or rebase guard, error logged but bead still closed
2. **Worker closes bead before merge** — bd close runs in worktree, merge happens after (or never)
3. **Worktree cleanup destroys branch** — even if cherry-pick failed, the branch is deleted, losing the commits forever
4. **No verification gate** — nothing checks that the commit actually exists on main before closing the bead

## Fix Design

### Guard 1: Verify commit on main before closing bead
In mergeAndComplete(), after cherry-pick, verify the commit exists on main with `git branch --contains <hash>`. Only call bd close if verified. If cherry-pick failed, leave bead open with a note.

### Guard 2: Never delete worktree branch if merge failed
In worktree cleanup, check merge status before deleting the branch. If the branch has commits not on main, preserve it and log a warning.

### Guard 3: Post-close verification
Add a periodic sweep (or hook) that cross-references closed beads with main commits. Any closed bead whose claimed commit is not on main gets reopened automatically.

## Files
Read: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:mergeAndComplete, pkg/dispatcher/worktree.go (or wherever cleanup lives), pkg/dispatcher/merge.go (if exists)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mergeAndComplete does not close a bead unless the commit is verified on main
- [ ] Worktree branch is preserved when cherry-pick to main fails
- [ ] Test: simulated cherry-pick failure → bead stays open, branch preserved

  UPDATE escalations SET status='acked', acked_at=datetime('now') WHERE id=? AND status='pending'

title: Claude Code TaskOutput uses tail -f which hangs on completed tasks
description:
Root cause: Claude Code's TaskOutput tool internally uses 'tail -f <file> | head -N' to read background task output. When a background task completes with fewer than N lines, tail -f blocks indefinitely waiting for EOF that never comes on a regular file.

Evidence:
- Multiple hanging tail -f processes found via ps aux
- PIDs 29661, 88100, 45929 all running tail -f on .output files for hours
- These are spawned by worker Claude subprocesses during ops review

This is a Claude Code internal implementation issue, not fixable in oro codebase.

Workarounds:
1. Avoid backgrounding tasks in ops review prompts
2. Use 'Read' tool instead of Bash for completed output files
3. Kill hanging tail processes manually
4. File bug with Claude Code team

Blocked: oro-lkc5 (this bead)

title: Dispatcher does not mark beads in_progress on assignment
description:
When the dispatcher assigns a bead to a worker, it does not call 'bd update <id> --status=in_progress'. This causes bd stats to report 0 in_progress while workers are actively executing beads. Some workers update status themselves but it's inconsistent — observed 3/7 assigned beads marked in_progress.

The dispatcher should mark the bead in_progress at assignment time (in assignBead or equivalent), not rely on the worker to do it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dispatcher calls 'bd update <id> --status=in_progress' when assigning a bead to a worker
- [ ] bd list --status=in_progress shows all beads with active worker assignments
- [ ] bd stats in_progress count matches dispatcher active_count
- [ ] Test: assign a bead to a worker, verify bead status transitions to in_progress

Read: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:assignBead, pkg/dispatcher/worker_pool.go
Signature: existing assignBead modified to include bd update call
Edges: bd update fails → log warning but do not block assignment
notes: 2026-02-16 13:09: PRIORITY_CONTENTION escalation for oro-wm6x demonstrates this bug — worker was assigned and actively working (PID 57369, worktree exists), but bead status remained OPEN instead of IN_PROGRESS, triggering false priority contention alarm.

title: Add one-shot claude -p manager as first responder for dispatcher escalations
description:
Add a one-shot manager tier between the dispatcher and the persistent interactive manager. When the dispatcher detects an escalation (STUCK_WORKER, MERGE_CONFLICT, PRIORITY_CONTENTION, MISSING_AC), it spawns a short-lived 'claude -p' process with a manager playbook + escalation context + recent history from the persistent escalation queue. The one-shot handles routine cases autonomously; unresolved escalations bubble up to the persistent manager.

## Open Design Question
How does the dispatcher know if the one-shot succeeded?
- Option A: Ack-based — one-shot must ack the escalation via CLI before exiting. Unacked = failed.
- Option B: State verification — dispatcher re-checks the triggering condition after process exit. Problem persists = failed.
- Option C: Both — ack proves agent tried, state check proves it worked.
Worker should evaluate and pick.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dispatcher spawns claude -p with manager playbook on escalation
- [ ] One-shot receives escalation type, bead context, and recent escalation history as prompt
- [ ] One-shot has access to oro directive and bd CLI commands
- [ ] Dispatcher detects one-shot failure and escalates to persistent manager
- [ ] One-shot timeout prevents runaway processes (e.g., 5 min max)
- [ ] Escalations that the one-shot resolves are marked acked in the persistent queue
notes: Decomposed into oro-pi5l → oro-jydf → oro-sh9f → oro-vi0h. Original too large (6 AC + unresolved design question). Closing parent once children complete.

Add a dev-sync target to the Makefile that copies assets/ to ~/.oro/ with explicit path mapping (not a flat copy). Add .envrc that triggers dev-sync on directory entry.

Path mapping (assets/ is NOT 1:1 with ~/.oro/):
  assets/hooks/     -> ~/.oro/hooks/
  assets/skills/    -> ~/.oro/.claude/skills/

  assets/commands/  -> ~/.oro/.claude/commands/

  source .venv/bin/activate 2>/dev/null
  if [ "$(git branch --show-current)" = "main" ] && [ -d assets ]; then
    make dev-sync 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi

dev-sync must:
  - Print what it copied (not silent)
  - Fail loudly on errors (no 2>/dev/null swallowing)
  - End with sanity check (verify at least one file at each target path)
  - Create target dirs if missing

title: Add restart-worker directive to kill and respawn a specific worker
description:
Add a 'restart-worker <worker-id>' directive that terminates a specific stuck worker, spawns a fresh replacement, and lets the dispatcher reassign the bead naturally. This is the surgical fix for STUCK_WORKER escalations.

## Implementation

1. Add `DirectiveRestartWorker Directive = "restart-worker"` to pkg/protocol/directive.go, update Valid().
2. In dispatcher.go applyDirective (line 1770), add case for restart-worker:
   - Parse worker ID from args string
   - Look up worker in d.workers map, capture its beadID
   - If worker has an assigned bead, return it to the queue (same logic as kill-worker)
   - Call d.GracefulShutdownWorker(workerID, timeout)
   - Spawn a new worker via d.procMgr.Spawn(newID) — target count stays the same (net effect: 1:1 replacement)
   - Return ACK with detail: 'restarted worker <id> → <new-id>, bead <bead-id> requeued'
3. If worker ID not found, return error ACK.

Depends on kill-worker bead for the shared 'return bead to queue' logic — extract a helper if both beads land.

## Acceptance Criteria
Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestApplyDirective_RestartWorker | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestApplyDirective_RestartWorker | Assert: old worker removed, new worker spawned, bead requeued, target count unchanged
Read: pkg/protocol/directive.go:Valid, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:applyDirective, pkg/dispatcher/worker_pool.go:GracefulShutdownWorker, pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:Spawn
Signature: func (d *Dispatcher) applyRestartWorker(args string) (string, error)
Edges: unknown worker ID → error 'worker not found'; empty args → error 'worker ID required'; spawn failure → error returned but old worker still killed (log warning)

title: Add kill-worker directive to terminate a specific worker
description:
Add a 'kill-worker <worker-id>' directive that terminates a specific worker and returns its bead to the ready queue. Currently the only way to remove a stuck worker is scale down/up, which is non-deterministic and disrupts healthy workers.

## Implementation

1. Add `DirectiveKillWorker Directive = "kill-worker"` to pkg/protocol/directive.go, update Valid().
2. In dispatcher.go applyDirective (line 1770), add case for kill-worker:
   - Parse worker ID from args string
   - Look up worker in d.workers map
   - If worker has an assigned bead, return it to the queue (unassign, set bead status back to open)
   - Call d.GracefulShutdownWorker(workerID, timeout) — do NOT respawn
   - Decrement target worker count by 1 (net effect: pool shrinks by 1, like a targeted scale-down)
   - Return ACK with detail: 'killed worker <id>, bead <bead-id> returned to queue'
3. If worker ID not found, return error ACK.

## Acceptance Criteria
Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestApplyDirective_KillWorker | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestApplyDirective_KillWorker | Assert: worker removed from pool, bead returned to queue, target count decremented
Read: pkg/protocol/directive.go:Valid, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:applyDirective, pkg/dispatcher/worker_pool.go:GracefulShutdownWorker
Signature: func (d *Dispatcher) applyKillWorker(args string) (string, error)
Edges: unknown worker ID → error 'worker not found'; empty args → error 'worker ID required'

title: Worker Claude process hangs on tail -f in TaskOutput
description:
During review, a worker's Claude process ran TaskOutput which spawned 'tail -f <output_file> | head -50'. The tail -f blocks indefinitely when the output file doesn't reach 50 lines, hanging the entire review phase.

Observed: PID 29661 running 'tail -f ...oro-rgux-18/tasks/b969d35.output' for ~2.6 hours on bead oro-rgux.18.

## Root Cause
TaskOutput uses 'tail -f' to follow a task output file. If the task completes with fewer lines than head expects, or if the task never writes enough output, tail -f blocks forever.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Identify how TaskOutput reads task output files and why tail -f hangs
- [ ] Add timeout or alternative read mechanism that doesn't block indefinitely
- [ ] Test: TaskOutput on a completed task with short output returns promptly

title: Dispatcher fails to detect Claude subprocess exit during review
description:
Workers in 'reviewing' state never transition out when their Claude subprocess exits. The worker Go process stays alive with zero children, holding a slot indefinitely.

Observed: workers for oro-l9gw and oro-zays.3 had no child processes but remained in 'reviewing' state for 2.5-3.5 hours.

## Root Cause
The dispatcher/worker does not monitor for Claude process termination during the review phase. When Claude exits (normally or abnormally), the worker should detect this and either retry or transition to idle/error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Worker detects when Claude subprocess exits during review phase
- [ ] Worker transitions to appropriate state (idle or error) on subprocess exit
- [ ] Worker reports subprocess exit to dispatcher with exit code/reason
- [ ] Test: simulate Claude exit during review, verify worker transitions within 30s

title: Fix architect_router.py: stop forwarding read-only commands to manager

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Fix inverted dependency graph direction in InsightsView

model.go:404-409 — buildInsightsModel filters dep.Type=='blocks' and takes DependsOnID, but this inverts the graph direction. If A blocks B, A's dep entry has DependsOnID=B, so B gets added to A's DependsOn list (meaning 'A depends on B'), which is backward. This makes critical path, bottleneck, and triage analysis produce wrong results.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Add persistent escalation queue with retry for dispatcher-to-manager messages
description:
The dispatcher sends escalations to the manager via tmux paste-buffer + send-keys (fire-and-forget). If the manager is interrupted (user input, context compaction, session clear), the message is lost. The dispatcher has no way to detect this and never retries.

The dispatcher already has a persistent store (state.db with an events table) and already uses file-based signals for the pane monitor (handoff_requested/handoff_complete). Escalations should be similarly durable.

Design options (worker should evaluate and pick):

Option A — Persistent queue in SQLite:
- Write escalations to a new escalations table (id, type, bead_id, message, created_at, acked_at)
- Dispatcher retries unacked escalations every N minutes via tmux
- Manager runs oro directive ack-escalation <id> after processing

Option B — File-based queue (simpler):
- Write escalations to ~/.oro/panes/manager/escalations/ as individual files
- Manager's SessionStart hook reads and displays pending escalations
- Manager deletes file after processing

Option C — Hybrid:
- Store in SQLite for durability and queryability
- Use file signal to wake the manager (like handoff_requested pattern)
- Manager reads pending escalations via oro directive pending-escalations

Key constraint: tmux paste-buffer is unreliable as a delivery mechanism. The solution must not depend on tmux delivery succeeding on the first attempt.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Escalations survive manager interruption/restart/compaction
- [ ] Unacknowledged escalations are retried (with backoff or periodic check)
- [ ] Manager can list and ack pending escalations via CLI
- [ ] No duplicate processing (idempotent ack)
- [ ] Existing escalation types (MERGE_CONFLICT, STUCK_WORKER, PRIORITY_CONTENTION, WORKER_CRASH) are routed through the new queue
notes: Implementation EXISTS in commit b4a8811 (merged to main). Escalations table schema, pending-escalations/ack-escalation directives, and retry loop are all implemented. False alarm on 'no code committed'. BLOCKED: Requires daemon startup to create escalations table via schema migration. Daemon has never been started on this system.

title: Externalize oro config: stop polluting target repos with .beads/.claude
description:
## Problem

Oro currently takes over the target project's `.claude/` directory and commits `.beads/` into git. This makes oro unusable in repos that already have their own Claude Code configuration, and pollutes project history with oro-specific files.

**What oro currently writes into the target repo (all tracked in git):**
- `.beads/` — issues.jsonl, interactions.jsonl, knowledge.jsonl, formulas, config, metadata
- `.claude/hooks/` — 15+ hooks (worktree guards, skill enforcement, context injection, etc.)
- `.claude/skills/` — 30+ skills (TDD, debugging, brainstorming, agent-browser, etc.)
- `.claude/settings.json` — hook configuration, tool permissions
- `.claude/commands/` — restart-oro, toggle-priming
- `.claude/hooks/beacons/` — architect.md, manager.md (role prompts)
- `docs/handoffs/` — session handoff YAML files
- `docs/decisions-and-discoveries.md` — architectural log
- `.claude/review-patterns.md` — code review patterns

**Why this is a P0:**
- Oro cannot be used in any project that has its own `.claude/` setup without stomping on it
- Every project oro touches gets 50+ committed files that have nothing to do with the project
- Makes oro non-portable — it's welded to the oro repo itself right now

## Prior Art: Gas Town

Gas Town (steveyegge/gastown) solves this cleanly:
1. **`--settings` flag** — Claude Code supports `claude --settings <path>` which merges a settings file additively with the project's own `.claude/settings.json`
2. **Parent directory trick** — places `.claude/settings.json` in a parent directory above the cloned repo; Claude Code walks up the tree and finds it
3. **Global config** — hooks/overrides live in `~/.gt/`, never in the target repo
4. **Role-based layering** — base config + role overrides + rig-specific overrides, merged at launch

## Proposed Architecture

```
~/.oro/                              # global oro home (XDG_DATA_HOME compliant)
  config.yaml                        # global oro settings
  skills/                            # skill library (shared across all projects)
    agent-browser/SKILL.md
    brainstorming/SKILL.md
    ...30+ skills
  hooks/                             # hook scripts (shared)
    enforce-skills.sh
    worktree_guard.py
    ...15+ hooks
  hooks-base.json                    # base .claude/settings.json template
  hooks-overrides/                   # per-role settings overrides
    architect.json
    manager.json
    worker.json
  beacons/                           # role prompt templates
    architect.md
    manager.md
  templates/                         # handoff/decision templates

~/.oro/projects/<project-name>/      # per-project persistent state
  beads/                             # issue tracker (currently .beads/)
    issues.jsonl
    interactions.jsonl
    memory/knowledge.jsonl
    formulas/
  handoffs/                          # session handoff YAMLs
  decisions.md                       # architectural log
  generated/                         # generated settings files for claude --settings
    architect-settings.json
    manager-settings.json
    worker-settings.json

<target-project>/                    # THE ACTUAL PROJECT — UNTOUCHED
  .claude/                           # project's own Claude Code config (if any)
  .gitignore                         # no oro entries needed
  src/
  ...
```

## Key Design Decisions to Make

1. **Settings injection**: Use `claude --settings` flag or parent-directory `.claude/settings.json`? Gas Town uses both — parent dir for hierarchy, --settings for explicit overrides.

2. **Skill discovery**: Claude Code discovers skills from `.claude/skills/`. If we move skills to `~/.oro/skills/`, how do agents find them? Options:
   - Symlink `~/.oro/skills/` into a parent `.claude/skills/`
   - Use `--settings` to inject skill paths (if supported)
   - Generate a CLAUDE.md that references skill content inline

3. **Beads CLI**: `bd` currently assumes `.beads/` is in CWD. Needs `--project` flag or env var (`ORO_PROJECT`) to find `~/.oro/projects/<name>/beads/`.

4. **Hooks**: Currently live in `.claude/hooks/`. With externalization:
   - Hook scripts go to `~/.oro/hooks/`
   - `hooks-base.json` defines the hook config pointing to those scripts
   - `oro init <project>` generates role-specific settings.json files
   - `oro start` passes `--settings` to each agent

5. **CLAUDE.md**: Currently checked into the project. Options:
   - Minimal stub in project: `See .oro/CLAUDE.md for oro instructions`
   - Inject via hook at SessionStart
   - Use parent directory CLAUDE.md (Claude Code walks up)

6. **Migration**: How to migrate the oro repo itself from embedded to externalized config.

7. **`oro init`**: New command that:
   - Creates `~/.oro/projects/<name>/` structure
   - Links/generates settings files
   - Optionally adds `.oro/` to project's `.gitignore`
   - Does NOT modify `.claude/` in the target project

8. **`oro eject`**: Reverse of init — remove all oro traces from a project.

## What NOT to Externalize

Some things might legitimately belong in the target project:
- Project-specific hooks (quality gate config?)
- Project-specific CLAUDE.md instructions
- `.oro/config.yaml` — local project oro config (gitignored)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Brainstorm session produces a design spec
- [ ] Design spec covers all 8 decision points above
- [ ] Design spec includes migration plan for existing oro repo
- [ ] Design spec addresses how workers in worktrees access externalized config
- [ ] Design spec addresses how `bd` CLI finds beads when not in CWD

title: Dispatcher auto-scale: increase targetWorkers when queue has beads and no idle workers

title: Auto-scale workers based on queue depth and notify manager of new beads
description:
## Problem

When the architect creates beads via \`bd create\`, the manager is not notified and doesn't scale workers. The dispatcher sees new beads (via fsnotify → tryAssign → bd ready) but can't assign them because \`targetWorkers\` is 0 or insufficient. Workers are only spawned when the manager explicitly runs \`oro directive scale N\`.

### Root cause chain:
1. Architect runs \`bd create\` → bead exists in \`bd ready\`
2. Dispatcher's \`assignLoop\` detects it via fsnotify → calls \`tryAssign()\`
3. \`tryAssign()\` calls \`filterAssignable()\` → finds beads
4. BUT \`tryAssign()\` only assigns to connected workers (dispatcher.go:1393-1410)
5. Worker count is controlled by \`targetWorkers\` (set via \`oro directive scale N\`)
6. Manager beacon only scales at startup (manager.go:27-37), no continuous monitoring
7. **No notification** from architect → manager that new work exists

## Design

Two-part fix:

### Part 1: Dispatcher auto-scale (primary fix)

After \`tryAssign()\` finds assignable beads but has no idle workers, auto-scale up to a configured max:

\`\`\`go
// In tryAssign(), after filterAssignable returns beads:
if len(beads) > 0 {
    d.mu.Lock()
    idleCount := countIdleWorkers(d.workers)
    maxWorkers := d.cfg.MaxWorkers // New config field, default 3
    currentTarget := d.targetWorkers
    d.mu.Unlock()

    if idleCount == 0 && currentTarget < maxWorkers {
        // Auto-scale: set target to min(len(beads), maxWorkers)
        newTarget := min(len(beads), maxWorkers)
        if newTarget > currentTarget {
            d.mu.Lock()
            d.targetWorkers = newTarget
            d.mu.Unlock()
            d.reconcileScale()
            _ = d.logEvent(ctx, "auto_scale", "dispatcher", "", "",
                fmt.Sprintf("scaled to %d workers (queue depth: %d)", newTarget, len(beads)))
        }
    }
}
\`\`\`

Add \`MaxWorkers int\` to \`Config\` (dispatcher.go:114). Default: 3. Set via \`oro start --workers N\` (already exists, maps to \`--workers\` flag in cmd_start.go).

### Part 2: Architect → Manager notification (awareness)

In \`architect_router.py\`, when a \`bd create\` command is detected (currently passed through since it starts with \`bd \`), ALSO send a notification to the manager pane via tmux:

\`\`\`python
# In route_command(), after identifying "bd create" commands:
if trimmed.startswith("bd create"):
    # Don't block — let it execute locally
    # But also notify manager
    notify_manager(f"[NEW WORK] Architect created a bead. Check bd ready.")
    return "architect"  # Still execute locally
\`\`\`

This is a PostToolUse hook on Bash (for \`bd create\` commands), not a PreToolUse block. It should be a separate hook or an addition to the existing \`architect_router.py\`.

## Files to Modify
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go — Add MaxWorkers to Config, auto-scale logic in tryAssign (near line 1410)
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go — Test auto-scale behavior
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go — Wire --workers flag to MaxWorkers config
- .claude/hooks/architect_router.py — Add PostToolUse notification for bd create (or new hook)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestAutoScaleRespectsMaxWorkers | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestAutoScaleRespectsMax | Assert: Auto-scale never exceeds MaxWorkers config value
- [ ] Dispatcher auto-spawns workers when beads are available and current workers < MaxWorkers
- [ ] Manager pane receives tmux notification when architect creates beads

Signature: Config.MaxWorkers int (default 3)

title: Clarify Claude Code LSP server requirement
description:
Research shows Claude Code does not have an LSP server feature.

**Research findings:**
- `claude --help` shows no `lsp` subcommand
- `claude lsp` is interpreted as a user prompt, not a command
- `--ide` flag is for Claude connecting TO an IDE, not serving as an LSP server
- No LSP-related binaries or documentation found in ~/.claude/

**Possible interpretations:**
1. Requirement is outdated - feature was planned but not implemented
2. Misunderstanding - maybe we should launch `--ide` flag to connect to user's IDE?
3. Different approach - use a different integration method?

**Action needed:**
Clarify what the actual requirement is for "Claude Code LSP server" in oro-15tz.

title: Add user-prompt-submit-hook to Claude Code for command interception
description:
The architect command forwarding feature (oro-9hd) requires intercepting user input before it's sent to Claude. Claude Code currently has SessionStart hooks but no user-prompt-submit hooks. Need to either: (1) contribute a user-prompt-submit-hook to Claude Code, (2) wrap Claude Code in a shell function/script that intercepts input, or (3) implement as a Bash skill that the architect manually invokes. Files: .claude/hooks/, cmd/oro/architect.go.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A hook or wrapper exists that receives the user's typed input before Claude processes it
- [ ] The hook can classify input as architect-bound vs manager-bound (e.g. commands prefixed with `/oro` or non-architect topics)
- [ ] Manager-bound input is forwarded to the manager pane via tmux send-keys
- [ ] Architect-bound input passes through to Claude unmodified
- [ ] Integration test: typing a forwarded command in the architect pane results in the manager pane receiving it
notes: AUDIT (oro-2h8q): Commit ed33f70 NOT on main. Superseded by architect_router.py (PreToolUse hook approach). UserPromptSubmit hook never needed — command routing achieved via existing Claude Code hook system.

title: Fix AC parsing: extract acceptance_criteria from description markdown
description:
The dispatcher's CLIBeadSource.Show() parses bd show --json into BeadDetail, but bd's JSON output has no separate acceptance_criteria field — AC is embedded as markdown in the description under '## Acceptance Criteria'. Since commit 0384b84 added checkBeadReady which guards on acceptance != "", ALL new bead assignments fail and escalate MISSING_AC. This blocks the entire swarm.

## Fix
In beadsource.go Show(), after parsing the JSON, extract AC from the description markdown (everything after '## Acceptance Criteria' header). Populate BeadDetail.AcceptanceCriteria with the extracted text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] BeadDetail.AcceptanceCriteria is populated by parsing the '## Acceptance Criteria' section from the description field
- [ ] If no AC section exists in description, AcceptanceCriteria remains empty (escalation is correct)
- [ ] Existing beadsource_test.go tests still pass
- [ ] New test: bd show JSON with AC in description correctly populates AcceptanceCriteria
- [ ] New test: bd show JSON without AC section leaves AcceptanceCriteria empty
- [ ] Workers can be assigned beads that have AC in their description

title: P0: missing_acceptance warn-through — assignment record created before validation
description: In dispatcher.go:1447-1454, createAssignment is called BEFORE checking acceptance criteria. If acceptance is missing, rejectMissingAcceptance cleans up worktree and resets worker state, but the DB assignment record was already created. Causes confusing logs and potential state inconsistency.
design: Fix: move acceptance criteria check BEFORE createAssignment and worktree creation. Check acceptance in the bead selection phase (Ready() or tryAssign) so beads without AC are never candidates for assignment.

title: P0: QG script missing in worktree — restore fails with exit 128
description: Worker finds quality_gate.sh missing in worktree, restore via 'git checkout HEAD -- quality_gate.sh' fails with exit 128. Likely caused by duplicate assignment (two workers in same worktree) or incomplete git worktree checkout. Worker.go:1001-1014 has restore logic but it fails.
design: Fix: 1) Verify worktree creation includes all files (add post-create validation). 2) Fix restore command — may need 'git checkout main -- quality_gate.sh' instead of HEAD if branch is new. 3) May resolve automatically once duplicate assignment is fixed.

title: P0: QG retry counter resets after model escalation — infinite loop
description: In dispatcher.go:707, attemptCounts[beadID] is unconditionally reset to 0 when model escalates to Opus. After escalation, counter restarts from 0, hits maxQGRetries again, escalates again (but already Opus), resets again — infinite loop. Workers never stop retrying.
design: Fix: only reset attempt counter on FIRST escalation (Sonnet→Opus). If already Opus and at maxRetries, mark bead as failed/stuck and release the worker. Add a totalAttempts counter that never resets.

title: P0: Duplicate bead assignment — both workers get same bead
description: Race condition in tryAssign (dispatcher.go:1319-1366): idle workers snapshot captured before assignBead, no re-check of worker state. Both workers end up on same bead (e.g. oro-js7.4) even when other beads are available. Root cause: lock released between idle snapshot and assignment loop.
design: Fix: hold lock through the assignment loop, or re-check worker.state==Idle inside assignBead before transitioning to Busy. Prefer the latter (finer-grained locking).

title: P0: QG exhausted for oro-js7.4
description:
Quality gate failed 3 times. Last output:
quality gate script not found: stat /Users/as21/codehouse/oro/.worktrees/oro-js7.4/quality_gate.sh: no such file or directory (restore failed: exit status 128)

title: P0: QG coverage tool produces malformed import path — blocks all bead completions
description: Quality gate coverage check fails with: cover: malformed import path 'oro/pkg/worker/worker.go:1080.2,1080.12 1 0oro/pkg/dispatcher': invalid char ':'. All go tests pass individually but the coverage profile is corrupted (null bytes in go test output). This blocks every bead from passing QG, creating infinite retry loops. Also: QG retry attempt counter stays at 0 (never increments), so qg_retry_escalated never fires.

title: P0: Manager agent sends stop directive killing dispatcher — env-based guard doesn't work
description:
## Problem
The manager Claude session runs 'oro directive stop' ~30s after startup, killing the dispatcher. The HumanApproved guard (13594a5) checks ORO_ROLE env var, but Claude Code's Bash tool spawns subshells that don't inherit exec env vars from the tmux pane.

## Root Cause
tmux pane runs: exec env ORO_ROLE=manager claude
Claude's Bash tool spawns: /bin/zsh -c 'oro directive stop'
The zsh subprocess gets a fresh env from the user's profile — ORO_ROLE is not inherited.

## Fix Options
1. Remove 'stop' from oro directive entirely — make it only available via 'oro stop' (SIGTERM)
2. Add --confirm flag required for stop directive
3. Use a token file (.oro/human-token) that only oro stop creates
4. Check parent PID chain to detect agent context

## Acceptance Criteria
- oro directive stop from manager agent must be rejected by dispatcher
- oro stop from human terminal must still work
- Test: run swarm, verify it stays up >5 minutes with workers assigned

title: Manager must never send stop-all without human approval
description: Manager Claude session sent stop-all directive autonomously, killing the entire swarm. Root cause: dispatcher.go:1491 applyDirective() accepts DirectiveStop unconditionally. Manager prompt (manager.go:139) only has a natural language warning. Fix: add guard in applyDirective() that rejects stop unless human-approval token is provided. Manager should only stop individual workers, not the swarm.
notes: Acceptance: Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestApplyDirective_StopRequiresHumanApproval | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestApplyDirective_StopRequiresHumanApproval -v | Assert: stop without HumanApproved returns error; stop with HumanApproved=true succeeds and transitions to StateStopping

title: oro cleanup CLI: kill tmux/dispatcher/workers, remove worktrees, reset orphaned beads
description: When oro crashes (tmux dies, dispatcher exits), everything is left in a broken state: orphaned beads stuck in_progress, stale PID files, dead worktrees, no processes. Need a single 'oro cleanup' (or 'oro nuke') command that: (1) kills tmux session if exists, (2) kills dispatcher process if running, (3) kills any worker claude processes, (4) removes stale PID/socket files, (5) resets all in_progress beads back to open, (6) cleans up any leftover git worktrees, (7) reports what it cleaned. Should be idempotent and safe to run anytime. Currently requires manual cleanup across multiple systems.

title: Pass --session-id to Claude launches in roleEnvCmd
description:
Multiple oro Claude sessions (architect, manager, human) share up-arrow input history because Claude Code keys history off the working directory. All three run in the same project dir, so pressing up-arrow in one shows messages from the others.

Fix: append '--session-id $(uuidgen)' to the claude command in roleEnvCmd() so each tmux window gets an isolated session ID.

Test: cmd/oro/tmux_test.go:TestRoleEnvCmd (new) + existing TestTmux suite
Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/oro/ -run 'TestRoleEnvCmd|TestTmux'
Assert: roleEnvCmd('architect') contains '--session-id'; command still contains 'claude' and not 'claude -p'; existing launch tests still pass
Read: cmd/oro/tmux.go:roleEnvCmd, cmd/oro/tmux_test.go
Signature: func roleEnvCmd(role string) string  (unchanged signature, changed body)
Edges: uuidgen not found on PATH → claude still launches but shares history (graceful degradation, not a blocker)

title: Fix ops review: non-zero exit code overrides APPROVED verdict
description: parseResult() in ops.go:249-253 returns VerdictFailed when waitErr \!= nil, even if stdout contains APPROVED. The ops reviewer (claude -p) exits non-zero sometimes even on successful reviews. Fix: when opsType is OpsReview and stdout contains APPROVED/REJECTED, trust the parsed verdict over the exit code. The text-based verdict is the reviewer's actual decision; the exit code is an infrastructure artifact. AC: (1) If stdout contains APPROVED and exit code is non-zero, verdict is VerdictApproved (2) If stdout contains REJECTED and exit code is non-zero, verdict is VerdictRejected (3) Only fall back to VerdictFailed if stdout has neither keyword (4) Test: simulate non-zero exit with APPROVED output, verify VerdictApproved

title: Add progress timeout to dispatcher (15min default)
description: Dispatcher only has liveness timeout (45s heartbeat). Workers can heartbeat for hours with no progress. Add lastProgress timestamp to worker struct, updated on DONE/READY_FOR_REVIEW/QG result/first STATUS after assign. Add ProgressTimeout config (default 15min). In checkHeartbeats, detect WorkerBusy workers where now-lastProgress > ProgressTimeout, escalate as STUCK_WORKER and kill. AC: (1) Workers idle >15min with no progress trigger STUCK_WORKER escalation (2) lastProgress updated on meaningful events (3) Test: simulate stalled worker, verify escalation fires

title: Include MemoryContext and Attempt in rejection reassign
description: handleReviewRejection sends ASSIGN back to worker but without MemoryContext (reviewer feedback history) or Attempt counter. Worker retries blind. Fix: build MemoryContext from rejection history, include Attempt count in ASSIGN message. AC: (1) Rejection ASSIGN includes reviewer feedback in MemoryContext (2) Attempt counter increments on each rejection (3) Test: verify ASSIGN payload after rejection
acceptance_criteria: Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestRejectionReassignIncludesMemoryAndAttempt | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestRejectionReassignIncludesMemoryAndAttempt | Assert: ASSIGN message after rejection contains MemoryContext with reviewer feedback and incremented Attempt counter

title: Clear pendingQGOutput on rejection reassign
description: worker.go handleAssign() resets sessionText but not pendingQGOutput. Stale QG output gets sent on next approval. Fix: add w.pendingQGOutput = '' in handleAssign(). AC: (1) pendingQGOutput is empty after rejection reassign (2) Test: set pendingQGOutput, call handleAssign, verify cleared

title: Fix worker zombie state after review escalation
description: After maxReviewRejections (2), handleReviewRejection calls clearBeadTracking() but leaves worker in WorkerBusy with stale beadID. Worker heartbeats forever, never gets new work. Fix: reset worker to WorkerIdle, clear beadID/worktree, kill subprocess. AC: (1) After 3rd rejection, worker transitions to Idle within one assign cycle (2) Worker gets new bead assigned (3) Test: simulate 3 rejections, verify worker state is Idle and beadID is empty

title: Fix duplicate bead assignment when scaling up workers
description: When the manager scales up (e.g. scale 5->6), the new worker gets assigned a bead that's already assigned to an existing worker. The dispatcher's assignLoop should check if a bead is already assigned before creating a new worktree. Symptom: repeated worktree_error events as the new worker tries to create a branch that already exists in an active worktree.
acceptance_criteria: Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestScaleUpDoesNotDuplicateAssignment | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestScaleUpDoesNotDuplicateAssignment | Assert: Test passes, no worktree_error events for duplicate assignments

title: Merge oro-nqi.2 scaffold to main
description: oro-nqi.2 was closed but agent/oro-nqi.2 branch was never merged to main. oro-nqi.3 and other child beads depend on this scaffold code being available on main. Commit f437c0b contains the scaffold.

title: quality_gate.sh missing from worktree checkout
description:
When dispatcher creates worktrees via 'git worktree add .worktrees/<bead> -b agent/<bead> main', quality_gate.sh should be present (it is tracked in git on main). But both oro-noc.1 and oro-nqi.2 workers got:

  quality gate script not found: stat /Users/as21/codehouse/oro/.worktrees/oro-noc.1/quality_gate.sh: no such file or directory

Possible causes:
1. The claude -p agent deleted/moved quality_gate.sh during its work session
2. The worktree was cleaned up before RunQualityGate ran (timing race)
3. The worktree checkout was somehow incomplete

quality_gate.sh IS in git (git ls-files confirms), so any fresh checkout from main should have it. Need to reproduce and check whether the file exists in the worktree immediately after creation vs after claude -p finishes.

Key code: pkg/worker/worker.go:995-999 — RunQualityGate stats the script path

title: P0: QG retry fails silently — worker connection dead before re-ASSIGN
description:
When a worker's claude -p finishes and the worker sends DONE with QualityGatePassed=false, the dispatcher calls handleQGFailure → qgRetryWithReservation, which tries to send a new ASSIGN back to the same worker. But the worker process has already exited after sending DONE — the connection is dead. sendToWorker silently fails, and no retry or escalation happens. The bead just disappears.

Observed: Both oro-noc.1 and oro-nqi.2 hit quality_gate_rejected, logged done, then silence. No re-assignment, no heartbeats, no escalation. Workers dropped to 0.

Root cause: The worker sends DONE and then exits its Run loop. By the time the dispatcher's qgRetryWithReservation sends the re-ASSIGN, the conn is closed. sendToWorker likely returns an error that is not escalated.

Fix direction: Either (a) the worker must stay alive after sending DONE with QG failure and wait for a re-ASSIGN or shutdown, or (b) the dispatcher must detect the dead connection in qgRetryWithReservation and re-queue the bead for a different worker (or the same worker after reconnect).

Key code paths:
- pkg/worker/worker.go:478-482 — worker sends DONE on QG failure then returns (exits)
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:611-670 — handleQGFailure increments attempt, reserves worker, calls qgRetryWithReservation
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:675-705 — qgRetryWithReservation sends re-ASSIGN to (now dead) worker

title: Fix BeadSource.Show JSON array parsing
description: bd show <id> --json returns a JSON array [{...}] but CLIBeadSource.Show() unmarshals into a single protocol.BeadDetail struct, causing json.Unmarshal to fail. This makes every bead assignment fail with 'bead X not found' — the dispatcher assigns beads but can never build worker prompts. Fix: unmarshal into []protocol.BeadDetail and take [0], or use json.Decoder to handle both forms.
acceptance_criteria: Test: pkg/dispatcher/beadsource_test.go:TestCLIBeadSource_Show_ArrayJSON | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestCLIBeadSource_Show -v | Assert: PASS

title: Enforce hard timeout on dispatcher shutdown sequence
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §3.5

**Problem:** If worker never responds to PREPARE_SHUTDOWN, shutdown can hang indefinitely.

**Design:** Wrap shutdownSequence in context.WithTimeout(2 * ShutdownTimeout). If hard timeout exceeded, force-close all connections and clear worker map. Run() returns within bounded time.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: TestShutdownHardTimeout | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: unresponsive worker doesn't prevent shutdown; Run() returns within 2*ShutdownTimeout

title: Add subprocess health monitoring to worker
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §3.4

**Problem:** Workers don't monitor if claude -p subprocess is alive between heartbeats. Hung subprocess (see oro-gzi) leaves worker appearing alive while doing nothing.

**Design:** Add periodic liveness check to watchContext. If subprocess died without sending DONE, send DONE(false) with error. May need Alive() method on Process interface or OS-level check.

**Files:** pkg/worker/worker.go, pkg/worker/worker_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: TestSubprocessHealthCheck | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/worker/... | Assert: killed subprocess detected within contextPollInterval, DONE(false) sent

title: Add stale socket detection before dispatcher bind
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §3.3

**Problem:** Previous crash leaves socket file. net.Listen fails with 'address already in use'. User must manually delete socket.

**Design:** Before listen: stat socket, try connecting (1s timeout). If connects = another dispatcher running (error). If fails = stale socket, remove it.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: TestStaleSocketCleanup | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: stale socket file removed, dispatcher starts; active socket returns error

title: Rework role identity: env vars + SessionStart hook instead of send-keys beacon
description:
Adopt the Gastown pattern for role identity. Currently oro puts all role differentiation weight on a fragile tmux send-keys beacon injection that silently fails for large payloads.

Gastown pattern to adopt:
1. Unique tmux session names per role (e.g. oro-architect, oro-manager instead of oro:0.0/oro:0.1)
2. Environment variables set at launch: ORO_ROLE=architect/manager, BD_ACTOR=architect/manager, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=architect/manager
3. SessionStart hook reads ORO_ROLE and injects role-specific context (architect beacon vs manager beacon) — no need for send-keys of huge strings
4. Separate working directories per role (or at minimum separate session storage)
5. Beacon becomes a small nudge/kick, not the entire role prompt

This replaces the current approach in cmd/oro/tmux.go where Create() sends the full ArchitectBeacon()/ManagerBeacon() (~100-150 lines each) via tmux send-keys.

Files to change:
- cmd/oro/tmux.go — session creation, pane naming, env var injection
- .claude/hooks/ — add ORO_ROLE-aware SessionStart hook that injects role context
- cmd/oro/architect.go — beacon becomes hook-injectable context, not send-keys payload
- cmd/oro/manager.go — same
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go — wire new session names

Reference: Gastown internal/config/env.go (AgentEnv), internal/session/names.go, SessionStart hook pattern.

title: Enforce WAL mode and db.Ping on production SQLite
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §3.2

**Problem:** WAL mode configured in tests but not enforced in production. Without WAL, concurrent readers/writers can deadlock.

**Design:** After sql.Open: db.Ping(), PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000.

**Files:** cmd/oro/cmd_start.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: Cmd: go test ./cmd/oro/... | Assert: PRAGMA values correct after startup
- db.Ping() called before any operations

title: Add orphan worktree cleanup on dispatcher startup
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §3.1

**Problem:** Dispatcher crash leaves .worktrees/ with orphaned directories. Never cleaned up on restart. Disk fills, stale branches pollute git.

**Design:** Add WorktreeManager.Prune(ctx). Runs git worktree prune, then removes all dirs in .worktrees/. Call from Dispatcher.Run() before starting accept/assign loops. Errors logged but don't prevent startup.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/worktree_manager.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/worktree_manager_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: TestWorktreePrune | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: orphan worktree removed on startup; no .worktrees/ dir = no error

title: Add context cancellation to GracefulShutdownWorker goroutine
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §1.5

**Problem:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go lines 1027-1075: Each GracefulShutdownWorker call spawns polling goroutine with no cancellation. Repeated shutdown attempts accumulate goroutines. Not tracked by WaitGroup.

**Design:** Use context.WithTimeout for the polling goroutine. Store cancel func in sync.Map keyed by workerID. Duplicate shutdown cancels previous goroutine. Track with WaitGroup from §1.3.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestGracefulShutdown_Cancellable | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: duplicate shutdown for same worker cancels previous goroutine, only 1 active
- Goroutine tracked by WaitGroup

title: Fix time.After timer leak in worker reconnect
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §1.4

**Problem:** pkg/worker/worker.go line 601: time.After(wait) creates timer that leaks if context cancelled during sleep. Each cancelled reconnect leaks a timer goroutine.

**Design:** Replace time.After with time.NewTimer + defer timer.Stop(). Select on both ctx.Done() and timer.C.

**Files:** pkg/worker/worker.go, pkg/worker/worker_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: pkg/worker/worker_test.go:TestReconnect_TimerCleanup | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/worker/... | Assert: cancel context during reconnect wait, no goroutine leak (check runtime.NumGoroutine delta)
- grep 'time\.After' pkg/worker/worker.go returns zero results (no time.After in production code)

title: Add sync.WaitGroup goroutine tracking to dispatcher
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §1.3

**Problem:** Dispatcher Run() spawns 3+ long-lived goroutines and N event-driven goroutines, tracks none with WaitGroup. Run() returns while goroutines still running — test flakes, resource leaks on shutdown, merge results lost. Also: acceptLoop spawns unbounded goroutines per connection (no semaphore).

**Design:** Add wg sync.WaitGroup to Dispatcher. Every go call: wg.Add(1)/defer wg.Done(). Run() waits wg.Wait() with 5s timeout before returning. Add bounded semaphore (100) for connection handlers in acceptLoop.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestRunWaitsForGoroutines | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: Run() does not return until all goroutines exit (within 5s timeout)
- Test: TestAcceptLoopBackpressure | Assert: 101st concurrent connection blocks until slot opens
- All go calls wrapped with wg tracking

title: Add defer to merge abortMu lock — prevent panic deadlock
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §1.2

**Problem:** pkg/merge/merge.go lines 72-83: abortMu.Lock() without defer. Panic between lock/unlock deadlocks all future Abort() calls permanently. In a merge coordinator handling rebase conflicts, panics are real.

**Design:** Wrap abortMu lock/unlock pairs in closure with defer. Both in Merge() setup (line 76-77) and the deferred cleanup (line 80-82).

**Files:** pkg/merge/merge.go, pkg/merge/merge_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: pkg/merge/merge_test.go:TestAbortMu_PanicSafety | Cmd: go test -race ./pkg/merge/... | Assert: panic between lock/unlock does not deadlock subsequent Abort() calls
- All abortMu.Lock() paired with defer in same scope

title: Replace lock-unlock-pray with two-phase reservation pattern
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §1.1

**Problem:** Dispatcher acquires mutex, reads state, releases for I/O (memory.ForPrompt), re-acquires, hopes nothing changed. checkHeartbeats can delete worker during unlock window, silently losing bead assignments. testUnlockHook exists to reproduce this — team knows it's broken. Affects: registerWorker (lines 388-450), handleQGFailure (lines 548-607), handleDone (lines 492-542), handleReviewResult (lines 860-904).

**Design:** Add WorkerReserved state. Under lock: set worker to Reserved (heartbeat checker skips reserved workers). Release lock for I/O. Re-acquire lock: verify reservation still valid, transition to Busy, send ASSIGN.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go:TestReservationPattern | Cmd: go test -race -count=5 ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: WorkerReserved state prevents heartbeat deletion during I/O window
- All 4 lock-release-relock sites converted
- testUnlockHook still works
- Existing tests pass unchanged

title: Epic: Lifecycle & Recovery
description: Fix silent data loss on crash. Orphan worktree cleanup, WAL mode, stale socket detection, subprocess health monitoring, shutdown timeout, dispatcher message buffering, escalation verification.

title: Epic: Concurrency Hardening
description: Fix data-loss and deadlock bugs in dispatcher and worker concurrency. Reservation pattern for lock-unlock-pray, WaitGroup for goroutine lifecycle, timer/goroutine leak fixes.

title: Fix beacon injection — use tmux load-buffer/paste-buffer for large payloads
description:
tmux send-keys silently fails or truncates when injecting large beacon text (ManagerBeacon is ~150 lines). The manager pane never receives its beacon — Claude just sits at the default prompt. The architect beacon may also have race conditions with PaneReady detecting the SessionStart hook's '>' as Claude being ready before it actually is.

Root cause: tmux send-keys is unreliable for large payloads.

Fix: Replace send-keys beacon injection with tmux load-buffer + paste-buffer pattern (write beacon to temp file, load into tmux buffer, paste into target pane). Also fix PaneReady to distinguish SessionStart hook output from actual Claude readiness.

Files: cmd/oro/tmux.go (Create method, lines 97-105 for beacon injection, lines 87-95 for PaneReady)
Reference: Gastown uses a similar buffer-based approach for large context injection.

title: oro start should attach to tmux session after launch
description: After oro start launches the dispatcher, architect, and manager in a detached tmux session, it should attach the user's terminal to the tmux session (like Gastown's gt mayor attach). Currently oro start returns to the shell and the user has to manually run tmux attach -t oro. Fix: at the end of runFullStart, wire stdin/stdout/stderr to tmux attach-session -t oro so the user lands inside the session. Reference: Gastown's attachToTmuxSession pattern in internal/cmd/crew_helpers.go.

title: Add oro init — bootstrap all dependencies and verify environment
description:
## Problem
There's no way to bootstrap oro. A fresh clone requires manually installing ~15 tools across Go, Python, npm, and system packages. oro start has basic preflight checks (tmux, claude, bd, git) but doesn't install anything or check the full toolchain.

## Design: oro init

New subcommand that:

### Phase 1: Check system prerequisites
- Go (>= version from go.mod)
- Python (>= 3.11)
- Node/npm (for biome)
- Homebrew (macOS) or apt (Linux)

If missing: print clear install instructions and exit non-zero.

### Phase 2: Install Go tools
- gofumpt (mvdan.cc/gofumpt@latest)
- goimports (golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest)
- golangci-lint (via go install or brew)
- go-arch-lint (github.com/fe3dback/go-arch-lint@latest)
- govulncheck (golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest)
- ast-grep (via npm or cargo)

### Phase 3: Install Python tools (via uv/uvx)
- uv itself (if not installed)
- ruff, pyright, pylint, pytest are invoked via uvx so no install needed

### Phase 4: Install system tools
- tmux (brew/apt)
- shellcheck (brew/apt)
- biome (npm install -g @biomejs/biome)
- jq (brew/apt)
- bd (beads CLI — check if installed, print install instructions)

### Phase 5: Verify
- Run each tool with --version
- Print summary table: tool | version | status (ok/missing/outdated)
- Exit 0 only if all required tools pass

### Integration with oro start
- oro start calls preflight checks (existing)
- Add flag: oro start --bootstrap to run init first
- If init hasn't been run (check for ~/.oro/.initialized marker), suggest it

### Behavior
- Idempotent — safe to run repeatedly
- --check flag: only verify, don't install (for CI)
- --quiet flag: suppress output, just exit code
- Respect platform (macOS vs Linux)
- Print what it's about to install before doing it

## Files
- cmd/oro/cmd_init.go (new subcommand)
- cmd/oro/cmd_init_test.go (test the check logic, mock installs)
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go (add bootstrap suggestion)

## Acceptance Criteria
- oro init installs all required Go tools
- oro init --check verifies environment without installing
- oro init prints clear table of tool status
- oro start suggests oro init when tools are missing
- Tests cover: all-tools-present path, missing-tool path, --check mode

title: Add post-injection beacon health check — verify Claude sessions received beacons
description:
## Problem
After beacon injection (tmux.go:83-89), nothing verifies the Claude sessions actually received and are processing the beacons. If injection silently fails (wrong pane state, Claude crashed, text truncated by tmux buffer), the swarm starts with lobotomized architect/manager sessions that don't know their roles.

## Current Flow
1. Inject beacon text via `tmux send-keys`
2. Return success immediately
3. `oro start` prints "swarm started" — no validation

## Desired Flow
1. Inject beacon text via `tmux send-keys`
2. Poll pane output for evidence that Claude is processing the beacon
3. For manager: look for `bd stats` execution (manager beacon step 1 runs this)
4. For architect: look for acknowledgment text or tool usage
5. Return success only after both sessions show activity
6. Timeout after 60s with clear error

## Design Notes
- Manager beacon instructs: "Run `bd stats`" as step 1 — we can watch for `bd stats` output in the pane
- Architect beacon is more passive — may need to look for Claude's "thinking" indicator or first tool call
- Use `tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane>` to read pane content
- This check runs AFTER readiness polling (depends on oro-XXX beacon readiness bead)
- Consider: should `oro start` print "waiting for sessions..." during this phase?

## Graceful Failure
- If manager doesn't start executing within 60s: print warning but don't kill the session (human can manually intervene)
- If architect doesn't show activity within 60s: print warning (architect is human-driven, so it may just be idle)
- Differentiate between "beacon not received" (no Claude activity) and "beacon received but execution slow" (Claude is thinking)
- Log the pane capture at timeout for debugging

## Files
- cmd/oro/tmux.go (add health check after injection)
- cmd/oro/tmux_test.go (test health check flow)
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go (integrate health check into startup flow, surface warnings)

## Acceptance Criteria
- After beacon injection, `oro start` polls for manager activity (bd stats output)
- Timeout produces a warning (not a hard failure) with diagnostic info
- Tests cover: healthy startup, manager timeout, pane capture failure
- `go test ./cmd/oro/... -run TestTmux` passes

title: Replace timing-based beacon injection with readiness polling
description:
## Problem
tmux.go:80 uses a fixed 2-second sleep before injecting beacons via `tmux send-keys`. This is fragile:
- If Claude hasn't loaded yet (slow startup, workspace trust dialog, MCP init), the beacon text lands in the shell prompt or nowhere.
- If Claude loads fast, we waste 2 seconds.
- There's no retry — if injection fails, the session is silently broken.

## Current Flow (tmux.go:48-93)
1. `tmux send-keys` to launch `claude` in each pane
2. `time.Sleep(2s)`
3. `tmux send-keys` to inject beacon text
4. No verification

## Desired Flow
1. `tmux send-keys` to launch `claude` in each pane
2. Poll pane content via `tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane>` until Claude's input prompt appears (look for the `>` prompt or `claude` text in the captured output)
3. Inject beacon text via `tmux send-keys`
4. Timeout after 30s with clear error message if Claude never becomes ready

## Design Notes
- `tmux capture-pane -p -t oro:0.0` dumps the visible pane content as text — grep for Claude's prompt indicator
- Claude Code shows a `>` prompt when ready for input. Look for this or similar indicator.
- Poll every 500ms, timeout at 30s
- Keep the `Sleeper` abstraction for testability — tests can inject a fake poller
- Add a `PaneReadyFunc` to TmuxSession that can be overridden in tests

## Graceful Failure
- If timeout: kill the tmux session, clean up PID file, return clear error: "Claude did not become ready in pane X within 30s — check workspace trust or claude installation"
- If one pane ready but other times out: still fail (both must be ready for the swarm to function)

## Files
- cmd/oro/tmux.go (replace sleep with poll loop)
- cmd/oro/tmux_test.go (update tests, add timeout test)
- cmd/oro/cmd_start.go (may need to pass timeout config)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Beacon injection polls for Claude readiness instead of fixed sleep
- Timeout after 30s with descriptive error if Claude not ready
- Existing tmux tests pass with updated mock
- `go test ./cmd/oro/... -run TestTmux` passes

title: Fix manager beacon startup sequence — skip 'oro start', go straight to directive
description:
## Problem
Manager beacon step 5 says: `Run oro start to launch the dispatcher (if not already running).`
But by the time the manager receives this beacon, `oro start` has ALREADY launched the dispatcher (it's what created the tmux session + injected the beacon). Running `oro start` again just prints "dispatcher already running (PID X)" and returns — the manager stalls.

## Root Cause
manager.go:35 — startup sequence assumes manager might need to start the dispatcher, but `oro start` always starts the dispatcher BEFORE creating the tmux session (cmd_start.go:64-84).

## Fix
Change the manager beacon startup sequence (manager.go lines 29-37) from:
```
5. Run `oro start` to launch the dispatcher (if not already running).
6. Run `oro directive scale N` to set the worker count to your chosen size.
```
To:
```
5. Run `oro directive status` to confirm the dispatcher is running.
6. Run `oro directive scale N` to set the worker count to your chosen size.
```

Also remove `oro start` from the Oro CLI section (line 43) or mark it as "used only by the human, not by the manager" since the manager never needs it.

## Files
- cmd/oro/manager.go (beacon text)
- cmd/oro/manager_test.go (update assertions if any reference the old text)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Manager beacon startup step 5 references `oro directive status` not `oro start`
- Manager beacon does not instruct manager to run `oro start`
- Manager test assertions updated to match new beacon text
- `go test ./cmd/oro/... -run TestManager` passes

title: Add dead code detection to quality gate — catch unwired exported functions
description:
Exported functions that are only called from tests pass the quality gate today. This is the root cause of the wiring gap pattern found in the brittleness audit — RunQualityGate, SendDone, SendReadyForReview all existed with passing unit tests but were never called from production code.

## What to add

A new tier in quality_gate.sh (between linting and testing) that detects exported Go functions only referenced from _test.go files. Options:

1. **deadcode** (golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode) — finds unreachable functions from main entry points
2. **unused** (honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/unused via staticcheck) — finds unused exported identifiers
3. **Custom grep check** — find exported funcs in pkg/, verify each has at least one non-test caller

The check should fail the gate if any exported function in pkg/ or internal/ has zero non-test references. Test-only helpers (SetContextPollInterval, SetReconnectInterval, etc.) can be annotated with a //oro:testonly comment to suppress.

## Why P0

This is not a feature — it's a safety net for the class of bug we just found 11 instances of. Every bead executed by a worker goes through the quality gate. Without this check, workers will continue building isolated functions that pass tests but aren't wired into the system.
acceptance_criteria: Test: quality_gate.sh detects that an exported function in pkg/ with no non-test callers fails the gate | Cmd: Create a dummy exported func in pkg/worker/ with only a test caller, run ./quality_gate.sh | Assert: gate fails with clear message identifying the unwired function

title: Investigate bash tool death after worktree removal
description: Bash tool becomes completely non-functional (every command returns exit code 1, no output) after git worktree remove --force when the shell's cwd was inside or related to the removed worktree. Happened twice this session: (1) after worktree removal + failed git rebase chain, (2) after worktree removal inside a chained command. Only recovers after user intervention (likely /clear or session restart). Root cause unknown — could be shell cwd invalidation, hook interaction, or sandbox state corruption. Need to reproduce reliably and add a safeguard. Workaround: never remove a worktree in a chained command — do it standalone, then verify bash works before continuing.

This prevents agents from pushing code that skips the full quality gate (pre-commit only catches per-file lint, not cross-cutting checks like golangci-lint, go-arch-lint, govulncheck). Also update the dispatching-parallel-agents skill and any agent prompt templates to include quality gate in bead completion steps.

This affects: (1) IPC design — Claude sessions don't natively speak UDS, may still need thin Go/binary wrappers for lifecycle but Manager itself is Claude. (2) All downstream beads: oro-w6n, oro-773, oro-r7b, oro-68t. (3) Manager now needs code search tools (full stack) for merge review. May still want daemons/binaries for plumbing, but they serve the Manager session, not replace it.

title: P4-5: Classify aggregate shadow read drift
description: Phase 4 epic closure review found ShadowStore aggregate read methods HasChildren and AllChildrenClosed route bool mismatches through compareValue, which always reports real divergence. During read-only shadow, primary-only writes can legitimately change child existence/closure state while SQLite lags, so these expected drifts must not be logged as real divergences.
