notes: Coordinator claimed 2026-04-28 from Phase 4 epic closure rejection. Scope: ShadowStore aggregate read divergence classification for HasChildren/AllChildrenClosed; avoid dispatcher/event viewer changes unless needed.
close_reason: Implemented aggregate shadow read drift classification in commit 45d3acfb. HasChildren and AllChildrenClosed now classify bool mismatches from exported child-row evidence with CLI parent_id export decoding, preserving primary returns; child updates during the shadow window report drift, while parent timestamp alone, stable pre-shadow mismatches, and read/export/decode errors report real. Worktree RED/focused test was confirmed by worker before implementation. Worktree verification: git diff --check main...HEAD PASS; go test ./pkg/beadstore/... -run 'TestShadowStore|TestShadowAggregateDivergence' -count=1 -v PASS; go test ./pkg/beadstore/... -count=1 PASS; go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -count=1 PASS. Adversarial review: initial design review caught parent timestamp risk; amended implementation to child-row classification; final review VERDICT: APPROVED. Ops review: timeout 480s claude -p exited 0 with terminal VERDICT: APPROVED. Main verification after cherry-pick: git diff --check HEAD~1 HEAD PASS; focused beadstore acceptance PASS; go test ./pkg/beadstore/... -count=1 PASS; go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -count=1 PASS. Residual: aggregate mismatch classification performs Export on both stores only when bools differ; accepted for shadow-only validation.

title: P4-4: Persist shadowStartedAt across restarts

notes: Coordinator claimed 2026-04-28 from Phase 4 epic closure rejection. Scope: persist shadowStartedAt in kv_store across selectStore/ShadowStore construction; preserve existing ShadowStore API/tests and dispatcher event logging.
close_reason: Implemented persisted shadow validation window in commit b73793eb (reviewed worktree commit cd5c6a37). Dispatcher shadow mode now creates kv_store on legacy DBs, load-or-initializes beadstore_shadow_started_at once with INSERT OR IGNORE, reuses the persisted RFC3339Nano timestamp across selectStore/dispatcher restarts, rejects malformed persisted timestamps fail-closed, and passes the value into ShadowStore via WithShadowStartedAt without changing NewShadowStore API. Tests cover one-time init/reuse, single-row persistence, drift classification from persisted window, legacy DB kv_store creation, malformed timestamp rejection, and existing ShadowStore behavior. Worktree tests: git diff --check main...HEAD PASS; go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -run TestSelectStorePersistsShadowStartedAt -count=1 -v PASS; go test ./pkg/beadstore/... -run TestShadowStore -count=1 -v PASS; go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -count=1 PASS; go test ./pkg/beadstore/... -count=1 PASS; go vet ./pkg/beadstore/... PASS. Adversarial review VERDICT: APPROVED. Ops review: timeout 480s claude -p exited 0 with terminal VERDICT: APPROVED. PASS. Residual: no explicit reset command implemented; spec says that is a future operator path and this bead prevents accidental resets.

title: P3-10: Reconcile apply pre-mutation backup

Implement a SQLite state backup before reconcile apply mutates state.db, print the backup path in reconcile report/output, and fail closed if backup creation fails before mutation.

title: Disambiguate oro start review timeout flags
description: The oro start --review-timeout flag currently feeds two distinct timeout concepts: the ops review subprocess timeout via ops.NewSpawnerWithReviewTimeout, and the dispatcher reviewing-worker stall timeout via dispatcher.Config.ReviewTimeout. These are different failure domains: one bounds the review process, the other detects a worker stuck in reviewing state. Sharing one flag/name makes operator intent ambiguous and can shorten or lengthen the wrong timeout silently. Preserve existing compatibility if needed, but make the two meanings explicit in CLI config, help text, tests, and daemon handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Test: cmd/oro/cmd_start_test.go:TestStartReviewTimeoutFlagsAreDistinct | Cmd: go test ./cmd/oro -run 'TestStartReviewTimeoutFlagsAreDistinct|TestStartProgressTimeoutFlag' -count=1 | Assert: oro start exposes distinct ops-review process and reviewing-worker stall timeout controls, both propagate to the correct config/spawner fields, and help text no longer describes one flag as both concepts.
notes: Implementation evidence: branch bead/oro-smzh0 commit 86ffa9b3697ecc64845715a4387fa03b7c3e4c58 splits --ops-review-timeout from --review-stall-timeout, keeps hidden --review-timeout stall alias, and propagates ops timeout to ops.NewSpawnerWithReviewTimeout while dispatcher ReviewTimeout receives stall timeout. Worker TDD red/green recorded. Coordinator verification: go test ./cmd/oro -run 'TestStartReviewTimeoutFlagsAreDistinct|TestStartProgressTimeoutFlag' -count=1 PASS; broader start tests PASS. Worker adversarial review exited 0 with VERDICT: APPROVED. Independent ops review exited 0 with terminal VERDICT: APPROVED. Residual risk: legacy --review-timeout no longer controls ops subprocess timeout; explicit --ops-review-timeout is now required.
close_reason: Implemented distinct review timeout controls in commit e63de7a0 (reviewed worker commit 86ffa9b3): --ops-review-timeout for ops subprocess, --review-stall-timeout for dispatcher reviewing-worker liveness, hidden --review-timeout stall alias. Verification after integration: go test ./cmd/oro -run 'TestStartReviewTimeoutFlagsAreDistinct|TestStartProgressTimeoutFlag' -count=1 PASS. Broader start tests passed in worktree. Worker adversarial review exited 0 with VERDICT: APPROVED. Independent ops review exited 0 with terminal VERDICT: APPROVED. Residual risk: legacy --review-timeout no longer controls ops subprocess timeout; use --ops-review-timeout explicitly.

title: Dispatcher must skip or quarantine ready beads with missing acceptance criteria

The dispatcher can stall with idle workers when bd ready returns a task that has no acceptance criteria. The dispatcher repeatedly raised MISSING_AC one-shot escalations for it; under Codex runtime those escalations failed, so no workers were assigned even though workers were connected and queue_depth was nonzero.

A malformed ready task must not block the assignment loop. The dispatcher should mark it non-assignable for the current scheduling pass and continue to later executable beads, while emitting a structured event explaining the skip/quarantine.

title: Fail loudly when inherited ORO_PROJECT conflicts with current repo
description:
Oro daemon commands currently allow an inherited ORO_PROJECT environment variable to silently override the project resolved from the current working directory. In practice this caused the Oro repo dispatcher restart to consult the scriptwriter project PID/socket because the tmux server environment still had ORO_PROJECT=scriptwriter.

Observed failure mode:
- cwd: /Users/as21/codehouse/oro
- inherited env: ORO_PROJECT=scriptwriter
- command: oro start/status/directive
- actual behavior: command resolves daemon paths under ~/.oro/projects/scriptwriter, reports or controls the scriptwriter daemon, or says a dispatcher is already running while the Oro project dispatcher is stale/dead.
- operational impact: stale pid/socket state, orphaned workers, beads stuck in in_progress, incorrect dispatcher status, and confusing restarts.

Desired behavior:
If cwd resolves to project A and ORO_PROJECT is set to project B, project-scoped daemon commands must fail loudly before reading/writing PID/socket/state for B. Error should name both projects and the cwd/repo root, and suggest unsetting ORO_PROJECT or cd'ing into the matching project.

Scope:
- Affects at least oro start, oro status, oro directive, and any helper that resolves daemon PID/socket paths for current-project operations.
- Do not remove ORO_PROJECT entirely; workers and intentionally project-scoped subprocesses still need it. The guard is for human/CLI current-project daemon commands where cwd gives a conflicting project identity.
- Preserve explicit override envs such as ORO_SOCKET_PATH/ORO_PID_PATH for tests only if they are already documented/used; they must not mask a real project mismatch in production paths.
acceptance_criteria:
Test: cmd/oro project resolution / daemon command tests | Cmd: go test ./cmd/oro/... -run 'Test.*OROProject.*Mismatch|Test.*ProjectMismatch|TestResolveDaemonPaths' -count=1 -timeout 120s | Assert: tests cover cwd project=oro with inherited ORO_PROJECT=scriptwriter and verify start/status/directive refuse to use scriptwriter PID/socket.
Read: cmd/oro/paths.go:detectProjectMode, cmd/oro/paths.go:readProjectNameCWD, cmd/oro/paths.go:ResolveDaemonPaths, cmd/oro/cmd_start.go, cmd/oro/cmd_status.go, cmd/oro/cmd_directive.go.
Edges: ORO_PROJECT matching cwd config remains accepted; ORO_PROJECT empty still resolves from cwd config/stealth project; worker/runtime code that intentionally sets ORO_PROJECT continues to work; error message includes env project, cwd project, and remediation.
Anti-pattern guard: do not merely unset ORO_PROJECT globally or ignore it everywhere. Implement an explicit mismatch guard at the daemon command/project resolution boundary so cross-project daemon control cannot happen silently.
close_reason: Tests pass: 8 new tests cover env/config mismatch scenarios for checkProjectMismatch and ResolveDaemonPaths. Quality gate green. Commit: 3ce68d29

title: Prevent quality gate mutation cleanup from wiping uncommitted work
description: scripts/quality_gate.sh runs mutation testing and then executes git checkout -- pkg/ internal/ cmd/ around lines 343 and 354. title: Detach dolt server from dispatcher process group (Setpgid)
description:
Bug: every `oro stop --force` kills the dolt server even though cmd_stop.go:357-358 documents 'dolt server is intentionally NOT stopped here. Dolt persists across sessions so standalone bd commands continue to work.'

Root cause: `startDoltServer` (cmd/oro/dolt.go:141-184) spawns dolt via `exec.CommandContext` + `cmd.Start()` with NO SysProcAttr. The dolt child inherits the dispatcher's process group and controlling-terminal session. When the dispatcher exits (via SIGINT from oro stop or natural termination), dolt receives SIGHUP/group signals and dies. The documented intent (persistence) is contradicted by the spawn behavior.

Empirical: observed 2026-04-25 — every oro stop produced 'warning: dolt flush: exit status 1' (the bd dolt commit racing the dolt termination), then bd commands failed with 'connection refused' until manual `bd dolt start`. Required during multiple architect-collapse swarm restart cycles.

Fix: insert `cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` before `cmd.Start()` in startDoltServer (between the CommandContext call at line 155 and the Start call at line 161). The existing reaper goroutine (`go func() { _ = cmd.Wait() }()` at line 181) continues to work — Setpgid only changes the child's process group, not the parent-child Wait relationship.
acceptance_criteria:
Test: cmd/oro/dolt_test.go:TestBuildDoltCommandSetsPgid | Cmd: go test ./cmd/oro/... -run TestBuildDoltCommand -count=1 -timeout 60s | Assert: extracted helper buildDoltCommand returns a *exec.Cmd whose SysProcAttr is non-nil and has Setpgid=true; existing startDoltServer behavior preserved (returns PID and writes pid/port files).
Read: cmd/oro/dolt.go:135-184 (startDoltServer), cmd/oro/dolt_test.go (existing test patterns), cmd/oro/cmd_stop.go:336-360 (where the bug manifests)
Signature: helper func buildDoltCommand(doltPath, beadsDir string, port int) *exec.Cmd (extracted from startDoltServer for testability)
Edges: Setpgid is Unix-only — guard the SysProcAttr assignment with build tags (//go:build !windows) if needed; macOS + Linux are the only targets oro supports per session context, so a single _unix.go file is sufficient. The reaper goroutine at line 181 is unchanged. PID file writing remains atomic with respect to Start. Tests must not actually spawn dolt (the test environment may not have it) — assert on the configured cmd before Start.
Anti-pattern guard: do not stub SysProcAttr setting with a comment-only change. The actual line must be present and the test must assert its presence. If extracting buildDoltCommand, the existing startDoltServer must call it (not silently bypass).
close_reason: Fixed in 6755ffa9. Setpgid:true added to dolt sql-server spawn via extracted buildDoltCommand helper. TDD test TestBuildDoltCommandSetsPgid asserts the configuration. Verified: gofumpt + goimports + go vet + go build clean.

title: Add periodic reconciliation of orphaned in_progress beads

title: Fix reranker JSON envelope parsing in ClaudeRerankSpawner
description:
oro index search fails silently (exit 1) because the reranker cannot parse Claude's --output-format json response.

## Root Cause
ClaudeRerankSpawner uses `claude -p --output-format json` which wraps the response in a JSON envelope:
```json
{"type":"result","subtype":"success","result":"```json\n[{\"id\": \"9\", ...}]\n```",...}
```

rerank.go tries to unmarshal the entire envelope as `[]rerankEntry`, which fails.

Three issues:
1. Spawner returns the full JSON envelope, not just the `result` field
2. The `result` field contains markdown code fences (```json ... ```)
3. Claude returns IDs as strings ("9") but rerankEntry.ID is int

## Files
- pkg/codesearch/claude_spawner.go — extract `result` from envelope, strip code fences
- pkg/codesearch/rerank.go — make rerankEntry.ID accept both string and int

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `TestClaudeSpawner_ExtractsResultFromEnvelope` — Spawn() given a JSON envelope returns only the inner result string with code fences stripped
- [ ] `TestRerank_ParsesStringIDs` — Rerank succeeds when reranker returns IDs as strings ("9") instead of ints (9)
- [ ] `TestRerank_ParsesIntIDs` — Rerank still works with int IDs (backwards compat)
- [ ] `TestRerank_EnvelopeParsing_EndToEnd` — Full round-trip: mock spawner returns real envelope → search returns ranked results
- [ ] `go test ./pkg/codesearch/... -v -count=1` passes

title: go-mutesting fails in worktrees — should skip gracefully

Fix: replace the blanket unset with targeted per-subprocess isolation, or re-export correct GIT_DIR after the unset.

title: Reset bead status to open when worker connection drops in handleConn cleanup
description:
## Bug

When a worker crashes (connection EOF), `handleConn`'s deferred cleanup (dispatcher.go:583-600) clears bead tracking maps via `clearBeadTracking(beadID)` but never resets the bead's status from `in_progress` back to `open`. The bead remains `in_progress` with no worker assigned, so:
- `isBeadAssignable()` rejects it (status != open)
- `bd ready` excludes it
- Idle workers have nothing to pick up
- The bead is stuck forever unless manually reset

## Root Cause

`handleConn` cleanup (dispatcher.go:583-600) is missing `d.beads.Update(ctx, beadID, "open")`. Compare with `applyKillWorker` (dispatcher.go:2540-2547) which correctly resets bead status before clearing tracking.

## Fix

In `handleConn`'s deferred cleanup, after capturing `beadID` and before/after `clearBeadTracking`, add:

```go
if beadID != "" {
    _ = d.beads.Update(context.Background(), beadID, "open")
    d.clearBeadTracking(beadID)
}
```

Note: use `context.Background()` since the parent ctx may already be cancelled (the connection dropped).

## Files
- `pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go` — `handleConn` deferred cleanup (lines 583-600)
- `pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go` — extend `TestHandleConnCleanupPrunesBeadTracking` to assert bead status is reset to open

## Acceptance Criteria
1. After worker connection drops, bead status is reset from `in_progress` to `open` via `BeadSource.Update`
2. `TestHandleConnCleanupPrunesBeadTracking` asserts `BeadSource.Update` was called with `(beadID, "open")`
3. Existing tests still pass (no regressions in `applyKillWorker` or normal DONE path)

title: Fix architect_router route_command default: keep shell commands local
description:
## Bug

`route_command()` in `.claude/hooks/architect_router.py` forwards ALL non-`bd` commands to the manager pane, including read-only shell commands like `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `cat`. The docstring says 'All other commands (ls, cat, etc.) stay with architect (safe default)' but the implementation does the opposite.

## Root Cause

Three defects in `route_command()` (lines 33-54):
1. Empty command returns `"manager"` — should return `"architect"`
2. No explicit check for build commands (`make`, `go build/test/install`) — they forward only because everything forwards
3. Default fallthrough returns `"manager"` — should return `"architect"`

## Fix

Invert the default in `route_command()`:
- `bd ...` → architect (existing, correct)
- `oro ...` → manager (existing, correct)
- `make ...`, `go build`, `go test`, `go install` → manager (NEW: explicit)
- `git ...` → architect (handled separately in `build_decision` via `_check_git_command`, but `route_command` should also return architect for consistency)
- Everything else → architect (CHANGED from manager)
- Empty → architect (CHANGED from manager)

Also update the docstring on `route_command()` to match the new logic.

## Files
- `.claude/hooks/architect_router.py` — fix `route_command()` function (lines 33-54)

## Tests
Tests already exist and describe the correct behavior — they are currently FAILING:
- `tests/test_architect_router.py::TestRouteCommand::test_unknown_commands_stay_local` — expects `ls -la` → 'architect'
- `tests/test_architect_router.py::TestRouteCommand::test_empty_commands_stay_local` — expects empty → 'architect'
- `tests/test_architect_router.py::TestRouteCommand::test_git_readonly_commands_stay_local` — expects `git status` → 'architect'

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `route_command('find /foo -name bar')` returns `'architect'`
2. `route_command('make test')` returns `'manager'`  
3. All tests in `tests/test_architect_router.py` pass

title: Dispatcher: merge worktree on bead_closed_externally when branch has unmerged commits

If no unmerged commits, cleanup proceeds as before (no change in behavior). 4. After the fix, externally-closed beads with completed work land on main rather than being abandoned on orphan branches. 5. Existing tests pass; a new test covers the bead_closed_externally-with-unmerged-commits path.

title: Dispatcher shows closed beads as in-progress indefinitely
description: When a worker completes a bead (closes it) and exits, the dispatcher's in-memory assignment table is never cleaned up. 'oro status' shows e.g. 'worker-xxx -> oro-i8i8.6 (STUCK, 4h58m ago)' even though the bead has been CLOSED for hours. The worker process may still be running (heartbeating) even after the bead is closed, suggesting the worker is not notified to exit after close. Root cause: dispatcher doesn't reconcile its in-flight assignment table against bead status from the DB. Fix: on each dispatcher tick, check if assigned beads are still open; if closed, unassign and signal worker to exit. title: Add go test to pre-commit hook for fast feedback
description:
## Problem

Pre-commit hook only runs formatting + lint (gofumpt, golangci-lint, ruff, shellcheck, biome, yamllint). Workers don't get fast feedback on test failures until the full QG runs, which includes the expensive mutation tier.

## Solution

Add go test to the pre-commit hook so workers catch test failures early, before the full QG with mutations runs.

## Files

- git/hooks/pre-commit: add go test -race -shuffle=on for staged Go packages

## Acceptance criteria

- Pre-commit hook runs go test on packages with staged .go files
- Test failures block the commit
- Only tests relevant to staged files run (not the full suite)

title: Skip mutation testing in pre-push hook (keep tiers 1-3)
description:
## Problem

Mutation testing is expensive. It already runs in the worker QG before merge. The pre-push hook runs the full quality_gate.sh including mutations — paying for mutations twice.

## Solution

Set ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1 in the pre-push hook before calling quality_gate.sh. Check that env var in quality_gate.sh to skip Go tier 4 (go-mutesting) and Python tier 5 (cosmic-ray). Pre-push still runs formatting, lint, tests, build, and security checks.

## Files

- git/hooks/pre-push: set ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1 before invoking quality_gate.sh
- quality_gate.sh: skip go-mutesting when ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1, skip cosmic-ray when ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1

## Acceptance criteria

- Pre-push hook sets ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1 before invoking quality_gate.sh
- quality_gate.sh skips go-mutesting (Go tier 4) when ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1
- quality_gate.sh skips cosmic-ray (Python tier 5) when ORO_SKIP_MUTATION=1
- Worker QG does NOT set ORO_SKIP_MUTATION — mutations still run before merge
- Tiers 1-3 still run in pre-push

title: Manager: push to remote after merges land on local main
description:
## Problem

Nobody in the oro system pushes to remote. Workers don't push (constraint in prompt). Dispatcher merges to local main via --ff-only but doesn't push. Manager beacon shutdown sequence says 'bd sync' + report status but never 'git push'. Architect doesn't touch git.

Commits accumulate on local main and never reach the remote until a human manually runs git push.

## Solution

The manager should push to remote. Two natural trigger points:

1. **After merge**: dispatcher notifies manager that a merge landed on main → manager runs git push
2. **Periodic**: manager pushes on a cadence (e.g. after every N merges or every M minutes)

Option 1 is simpler and more immediate. The dispatcher already sends status messages to the manager via tmux send-keys — add a MERGE_COMPLETE message type that triggers the manager to push.

## Key context

- Dispatcher merge: pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:934 mergeAndComplete()
- Manager beacon: cmd/oro/manager.go (no push in shutdown sequence either)
- Pre-push hook: git/hooks/pre-push runs full quality_gate.sh (all 4 tiers including mutation testing)
- Worker QG: pkg/worker/worker.go:1095 RunQualityGate() also runs full quality_gate.sh
- Architecture spec (docs/plans/2026-02-08-oro-architecture-spec.md:254) says shutdown step 4 is 'bd sync, git push' but this was never wired

## Acceptance criteria

- Manager pushes to remote after merges land on local main
- Manager beacon includes push responsibility in its protocol
- Manager shutdown sequence includes git push before reporting final status
- Pre-push hook (quality_gate.sh) runs on push and blocks if QG fails

title: Systematic closed-bead audit: verify all 50 beads have code/tests on main
description:
# Plan: Systematic Closed-Bead Audit

## Context

The user suspects some beads were marked closed without the work actually being done — a risk when agents close their own beads. We've already done a partial investigation and found concrete evidence of at least 3 missing tests and 1 bead closed with only "Closed" as a reason (no commit, no evidence). The goal is a systematic, parallelized audit that produces a verified list of: (a) confirmed complete, (b) satisfied differently, (c) falsely closed.

**Key findings from initial investigation:**
- **591 closed beads total** (`bd list` default cap is 50 — initial audit only saw the most recent 50)
- Of the first 50 examined: 13 had no commit hash in close_reason
- Worktrees (`/.worktrees/oro-b7l4/`) pollute grep results — must exclude
- 3 AC-required test functions are **missing from main**:
  - `TestCherryPickToMain_DerivesPrimaryRepo` — required by `oro-l6pz`
  - `TestOneShotEscalation` — required by `oro-sh9f.7`
  - `TestOneShotExitDetection` — required by `oro-sh9f.6`
- `oro-mzk0` closed with just "Closed" — most suspicious, no commit
- `TestOneShotTimeout` exists but **renamed** to `TestOneShotTimeoutEscalatesToPersistentManager` — AC matching must allow for renames

---

## Approach

Three phases, parallelized at Phase 2.

### Phase 1: Automated scan (single script)

Write and run an audit script (`ad_hoc/audit_closed_beads.py`) that:

1. `bd list --status=closed --json --limit 0` → parse **all 591** closed beads (default cap is 50 — must override)
2. For each bead, extract from `acceptance_criteria`:
   - All `Test[A-Z]\w+` function names
   - All commit hashes (40 or 7 hex chars)
3. For each test name: `grep -r "func <TestName>" /repo --include="*.go" --exclude-dir=".worktrees" -l`
4. For each commit hash: `git cat-file -t <hash>` + `git merge-base --is-ancestor <hash> HEAD`
5. Output: per-bead verdict table — PASS / MISSING-TEST / MISSING-COMMIT / NO-EVIDENCE

Script location: `ad_hoc/audit_closed_beads.py`
Output: printed verdict table + JSON summary to stdout

### Phase 2: Parallel deep investigation

Launch **one subagent per flagged bead** (expected: 4-8 beads). Each agent receives:
- The bead ID, title, full AC, close_reason
- The specific test name(s) that are missing
- Task: determine if work was done differently (renamed test, different file, merged under different bead), or genuinely missing

Each agent returns one of:
- `CONFIRMED_FALSE`: work not done, test missing, no alternative evidence
- `SATISFIED_DIFFERENTLY`: work done but via different test/file/commit — document how
- `NEEDS_HUMAN`: ambiguous, needs user judgment

**Known flagged beads to investigate in parallel:**
1. `oro-l6pz` — `TestCherryPickToMain_DerivesPrimaryRepo` missing (commit ef3d450 exists)
2. `oro-sh9f.7` — `TestOneShotEscalation` missing
3. `oro-sh9f.6` — `TestOneShotExitDetection` missing
4. `oro-mzk0` — "Closed" reason, no commit, no specific test
5. `oro-wee1` — "Merged to main, QG passed" but no commit hash
6. `oro-xhio` — same pattern as oro-wee1
7. `oro-c1wl` — nolint fix, no commit
8. `oro-atv5` — auto_load_skills path fix, no commit

### Phase 3: Action

For each `CONFIRMED_FALSE` bead:
- Reopen it: `bd update <id> --status=open` (or create new replacement bead)
- Add a note documenting what's actually missing
- File a new bead for the missing test if it's a test-only gap

For `SATISFIED_DIFFERENTLY`:
- Add a note to the bead explaining how it was actually satisfied
- No action needed (bead stays closed)

For `NEEDS_HUMAN`:
- Present to user with evidence and ask for judgment

---

## Execution Steps

1. **Write `ad_hoc/audit_closed_beads.py`** — the scan script
2. **Run it** — get the verdict table
3. **Read results** — identify all MISSING-TEST / NO-EVIDENCE beads
4. **Launch parallel subagents** — one per flagged bead (use `dispatching-parallel-agents` skill)
5. **Collect verdicts** — read each agent's output
6. **Execute actions** — reopen confirmed-false beads, file follow-up beads for missing tests
7. **Report to user** — summary of findings and actions taken

---

## Script Design (ad_hoc/audit_closed_beads.py)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Audit closed beads: verify AC-specified tests exist on main."""
import json, re, subprocess, sys

REPO = "/Users/as21/codehouse/oro"
EXCLUDE = ["--exclude-dir=.worktrees", "--exclude-dir=archive"]

result = subprocess.run(["bd", "list", "--status=closed", "--json", "--limit", "0"],
                        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
beads = json.loads(result.stdout)

results = []
for b in beads:
    ac = (b.get("acceptance_criteria") or "") + " " + (b.get("description") or "")
    test_names = list(set(re.findall(r"Test[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]+", ac)))

    verdict = "NO-AC-TESTS"
    missing, found = [], []
    for name in test_names:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["grep", "-r", f"func {name}", REPO, "--include=*.go", "-l"] + EXCLUDE,
            capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.stdout.strip():
            found.append(name)
        else:
            missing.append(name)

    if test_names:
        verdict = "FAIL" if missing else "PASS"

    results.append({
        "id": b["id"],
        "title": b["title"][:50],
        "verdict": verdict,
        "missing": missing,
        "found": found,
        "close_reason_snippet": (b.get("close_reason") or "")[:80],
    })

# Print table
print(f"{'ID':<15} {'VERDICT':<8} {'MISSING TESTS'}")
for r in results:
    flag = "🔴" if r["verdict"] == "FAIL" else ("⚠️ " if r["verdict"] == "NO-AC-TESTS" else "✅")
    missing_str = ", ".join(r["missing"]) if r["missing"] else ""
    print(f"{flag} {r['id']:<13} {r['verdict']:<8} {missing_str}")

# Summary
fails = [r for r in results if r["verdict"] == "FAIL"]
print(f"\n{len(fails)} beads with missing tests:")
for f in fails:
    print(f"  {f['id']}: {f['missing']}")
    print(f"    close_reason: {f['close_reason_snippet']}")
```

title: oro start leaves daemon orphaned when tmux session creation fails
description:
runFullStart (cmd/oro/cmd_start.go:98) spawns the daemon at line 113 via spawner.SpawnDaemon(), then waits for the socket, then calls sess.Create() at line 143. If sess.Create() returns an error (e.g. beacon timeout, tmux server not running, Claude crashes before beacon), the function returns the error — but the daemon is already alive and keeps running. oro status shows 'dispatcher: running' but tmux attach -t oro gives 'no sessions'. User must manually run oro stop to recover.

Observed: ran oro start --detach from Claude Code Bash tool (no default tmux server); dispatcher PID 63249 started fine, sess.Create() failed (no tmux server on default socket), daemon kept running, status showed running but no oro session existed.

Fix: add killFn func(int) error parameter to runFullStart (injectable for tests). After sess.Create() fails, call killFn(pid) as best-effort before returning the error. Production wiring: pass syscall.Kill-based fn in the cobra RunE at line 254.

Read: cmd/oro/cmd_start.go:runFullStart (lines 98-164), cmd/oro/cmd_start.go:ExecDaemonSpawner.SpawnDaemon (lines 38-64), cmd/oro/cmd_stop.go:killFn pattern (lines 26,68,175-177)

Signature: func runFullStart(w io.Writer, workers int, model, project string, spawner DaemonSpawner, tmuxRunner CmdRunner, killFn func(int) error, socketTimeout time.Duration, sleeper func(time.Duration), beaconTimeout time.Duration, detach bool) error

Edges:
- killFn returns error (daemon already exited) -> swallow error, log warning, still return the original sess.Create error
- daemon exits before cleanup attempt -> killFn will error, treat as no-op
- beaconTimeout=0 (defaultBeaconTimeout=60s) -> sess.Create hangs 60s before failing; cleanup still fires

title: Filter stale attempt counts from status response for closed beads
description:
## Problem
`oro status` shows "QG failed Nx" alerts for beads that are already closed (e.g., oro-9hd, oro-5srh.3). The dispatcher never clears `attemptCounts` entries when beads are closed externally via `bd close`.

## Root Cause
`buildStatusJSON()` (dispatcher.go:1917-1924) copies ALL `attemptCounts` entries into the status response without filtering. `pruneStaleTracking()` (bead_tracker.go:78) only prunes entries for beads not assigned to any worker — it never cross-references the bead source to check if a bead is closed.

Three scenarios create stale entries:
1. Bead fails QG, gets escalated, then closed externally — count persists because `clearBeadTracking` only runs on internal terminal paths
2. Bead fails QG, is between retries (no worker assigned), then closed externally — prune catches this eventually, but only on next heartbeat tick
3. Bead is closed while still assigned to a worker — prune skips it because worker is still active

## Fix
Enhance `pruneStaleTracking()` to cross-reference the bead source. Any tracked bead that is not in `d.beads.Ready()` AND not assigned to any worker should be pruned. This covers all three scenarios on the next heartbeat tick.

Alternatively (or additionally): in `buildStatusJSON()`, when copying `attemptCounts`, filter against the set of assigned beads + queued beads. This gives immediate accuracy in the status response.

## Files
- pkg/dispatcher/bead_tracker.go:78 — `pruneStaleTracking()`: add bead source cross-reference
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1917-1924 — `buildStatusJSON()`: filter stale counts
- pkg/dispatcher/bead_tracker_test.go — test pruning of closed beads

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: bead with attemptCounts entry but closed in bead source → pruned from tracking maps within one heartbeat cycle
- [ ] Test: `buildStatusJSON` does not include attempt counts for beads not in ready queue and not assigned to any worker
- [ ] Existing pruneStaleTracking tests still pass

title: Fix stale handoff_requested signal persisting across sessions
description:
## Problem
The pane_handoff_reminder.py PreToolUse hook fires on EVERY tool call in new sessions because
~/.oro/panes/<role>/handoff_requested signal file persists across sessions. The dispatcher's
restartPane() cleans it, but only during explicit pane restarts — not when a user starts a
new manual session. Result: every tool call gets a "CRITICAL: Context threshold reached"
warning even at 17% context.

## Root Cause
1. Dispatcher creates handoff_requested when context_pct exceeds threshold
2. Session ends (terminal closed, /clear, etc.)
3. New session starts — signal file still exists
4. pane_handoff_reminder.py checks file existence only, no context_pct guard
5. Every PreToolUse injects the critical warning

## Fix (two layers)

### Layer 1: SessionStart cleanup (session_start_extras.py)
In main(), after determining oro_role, delete handoff_requested if it exists:
```python
# Clean stale handoff signals from previous session
if oro_role:
    signal = Path(PANES_DIR) / oro_role / "handoff_requested"
    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
        signal.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```
Insert after line ~497 (after `oro_role = os.environ.get("ORO_ROLE", "")`).

### Layer 2: Defense-in-depth guard (pane_handoff_reminder.py)
Also check context_pct before firing. Only inject the warning if context_pct > 40:
```python
# Guard: only fire if context_pct is actually high
context_pct_file = panes_dir / role / "context_pct"
try:
    pct = int(context_pct_file.read_text().strip())
    if pct < 40:
        return  # Signal is stale, context is fresh
except (OSError, ValueError):
    return  # Can't read pct, don't fire
```
Insert in main() after _check_signal() returns True, before building the context string.

## Files
- assets/hooks/session_start_extras.py (add cleanup in main)
- assets/hooks/pane_handoff_reminder.py (add context_pct guard)
- ~/.oro/hooks/session_start_extras.py (installed copy)
- ~/.oro/hooks/pane_handoff_reminder.py (installed copy)
- tests/test_pane_handoff_reminder.py or similar (new test)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New session cleans up handoff_requested signal on SessionStart
- [ ] pane_handoff_reminder only fires when context_pct > 40%
- [ ] Test: signal file exists + context_pct=19 → hook returns no output
- [ ] Test: signal file exists + context_pct=55 → hook returns critical warning

title: Improve handoff mechanism to prevent empty context and missing AC in continuation beads
description:
Workers create continuation beads with empty 'Context from last handoff:' and no acceptance criteria, causing:
- New workers start from scratch with zero guidance
- MISSING_AC escalations from dispatcher
- Zombie beads proliferate (12+ cleaned this session)
- Handoff loops: oro-sh9f -> .1 -> .1.1 -> .1.2 (all empty context)

## Root Cause Analysis (verified against code)

Three locations create continuation beads, none pass acceptance criteria:

### 1. prompt.go:79-80 — Agent-initiated handoff
Template instructs agent to run: bd create --title="Continue: <bead-title>" --type=task --description="Remaining: <what's left>"
Missing: --acceptance-criteria flag, --parent flag, instructions to copy parent AC.

### 2. dispatcher.go:1048-1058 — handleHandoff() exhaustion path
Creates continuation via d.beads.Create() with only ContextSummary (often empty).
Never calls lookupBeadDetail() to get parent AC. No AC parameter in Create() signature.

### 3. beadsource.go:104-115 — CLIBeadSource.Create()
Function signature has no AC parameter at all. bd create command never gets --acceptance-criteria.

## Fix Design

### Fix 1: Add AC parameter to CLIBeadSource.Create() (beadsource.go)
Add `acceptanceCriteria string` parameter. When non-empty, append `--acceptance-criteria=<ac>` to bd create args.
Update BeadSource interface in dispatcher.go:60 to match.

### Fix 2: Pass parent AC in handleHandoff() (dispatcher.go:1048-1058)
Before creating continuation, call lookupBeadDetail(ctx, beadID, workerID) to get parent title + AC.
Pass AC to d.beads.Create(). Include parent title in continuation description for context.

### Fix 3: Update prompt template (prompt.go:79-80)
Change agent handoff instructions to include --parent and --acceptance-criteria flags.
Template should be: bd create --title="Continue: <bead-title>" --type=task --parent=<bead-id> --description="Remaining: <what's left>" --acceptance-criteria="<copy parent AC>"

## Evidence
oro-sh9f, oro-5srh.1, oro-ycjj.1.1, oro-ldbd.1, oro-mcxf.1, oro-5srh.3.1 all had empty handoff contexts.
lookupBeadDetail() already exists at dispatcher.go:1753 and is used in review path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Continuation beads created by handoff include parent AC
- Continuation beads include bead title from parent
- Worker context is never empty when picking up a continuation bead
notes: Decomposed: 3 separate fixes at different locations (beadsource, dispatcher, prompt) each need distinct tests

title: Allow architect to commit markdown and sync beads
description:
The architect_router.py PreToolUse hook currently blocks all Bash commands from the architect pane. This prevents the architect from committing its own output (specs in docs/plans/, decisions in ~/.oro/projects/, handoff YAML). The human has to manually commit architect work, which breaks flow.

Relax the hook to allow:
- git add *.md *.yaml *.yml (markdown and YAML only)
- git commit (when only markdown/YAML files are staged)
- git status, git diff, git log (read-only git commands)
- bd sync, bd create, bd update, bd close, bd list, bd show, bd ready, bd stats (all beads commands)
- git push (after committing markdown/beads only)

Continue blocking:
- git add on .go, .py, .sh, .js, .ts or any code files
- git commit when code files are staged
- make, go build, go test, go install
- Any command that modifies code

Implementation: in architect_router.py, add an allowlist check before the block/route decision. Parse the command to detect git add/commit/push with only markdown/YAML targets. Use git diff --cached --name-only to verify staged files are markdown-only before allowing commit.

- [ ] Architect can run: git add docs/plans/foo.md && git commit -m 'docs: add spec'
- [ ] Architect can run: bd sync && git push
- [ ] Architect CANNOT run: git add cmd/oro/foo.go
- [ ] Architect CANNOT run: git commit when .go/.py/.sh files are staged
- [ ] Architect CAN run: git status, git log, git diff (read-only)

title: Pane context lifecycle: file-based monitoring with automated handoff and restart
description:
Architect/manager have zero context exhaustion handling. Workers have full automated lifecycle (heartbeat → threshold → handoff → respawn). This epic adds the same for panes.

Design: File-based context monitoring. PostToolUse hook writes context_pct to ~/.oro/panes/<role>/context_pct. Dispatcher polls, writes handoff_requested signal on threshold. PreToolUse hook injects system reminder forcing create-handoff. Agent writes handoff to ~/.oro/panes/<role>/handoff.yaml. Dispatcher detects completion, kills tmux pane, relaunches. SessionStart hook reads per-role handoff on startup.

Key decisions:
- File-based (not UDS) — agents are interactive Claude sessions, not Go processes with persistent connections
- Per-role paths under ~/.oro/panes/ — separates automated recovery from human-readable docs/handoffs/
- Event-based restart: handoff creation triggers kill+restart, not a timer
- If human is interacting, they manage handoff themselves

## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed. Architect and manager automatically create handoff when context threshold reached. Dispatcher kills and restarts the pane. Restarted agent picks up latest handoff. Manual testing: run oro start, exhaust context, verify restart cycle.

title: Add process group isolation and kill to worker ProcessManager
description:
Problem: ExecProcessManager.Kill() only signals the worker PID directly. Worker spawns "claude -p" which spawns node → bash → arbitrary commands. Killing worker PID leaves node/bash children orphaned, holding worktree file locks and consuming resources.

Fix two things:
1. Spawn: Set SysProcAttr.Setpgid=true so each worker gets its own process group (CRITICAL: without this, killing PGID kills ALL workers + dispatcher)
2. Kill: Get PGID from spawned process, kill entire process group with syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGTERM), wait 3s grace, then syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)

Gastown pattern: KillSessionWithProcesses does PGID kill + recursive descendant walk. We skip the descendant walk (overkill for UDS workers) but adopt the PGID isolation + group kill.

Test: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager_test.go:TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Assert: spawned process with Setpgid=true; after Kill(), no processes remain in the worker process group
Read: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:Spawn,Kill,ExecProcessManager, cmd/oro/cmd_start.go:SpawnDaemon (reference for Setsid pattern)
Signature: unchanged public API; internal change to Spawn (add SysProcAttr) and Kill (add syscall.Kill(-pgid, sig))
Edges: Setpgid fails on non-Unix → build tag or runtime check; PGID=0 or PGID=1 → skip group kill (safety); worker already exited → ESRCH from kill, ignore
acceptance_criteria: Test: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager_test.go:TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/dispatcher/ -run TestKill_KillsProcessGroup | Assert: (1) spawned process uses Setpgid=true for process group isolation, (2) after Kill() completes, no processes remain in the worker process group

title: Detect and kill zombie tmux sessions in oro start
description:
Bug: TmuxSession.Create() has "if s.Exists() { return nil }". If previous oro start crashed leaving tmux alive but Claude dead, next oro start silently no-ops on a broken session. User must manually "tmux kill-session -t oro".

Fix: Before returning nil on Exists(), check if Claude is actually running via pane_current_command (same pattern as WaitForCommand). If session exists but Claude is dead in both panes, kill session and proceed with fresh creation.

Gastown pattern: EnsureSessionFresh — checks IsAgentAlive, kills zombie, creates fresh.

Test: cmd/oro/tmux_test.go:TestCreate_KillsZombieSession | Cmd: go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/oro/ -run TestCreate_KillsZombie | Assert: when session exists but pane_current_command returns "zsh" (shell, not claude), session is killed and recreated
Read: cmd/oro/tmux.go:Create,Exists,WaitForCommand,isShell, cmd/oro/tmux_test.go
Signature: func (s *TmuxSession) isSessionZombie() bool
Edges: session not found → not zombie (fresh create); pane_current_command errors → treat as zombie (conservative); session healthy → return nil (no-op as before)
acceptance_criteria: TestCreate_KillsZombieSession passes: session with dead Claude (pane_current_command='zsh') is killed and recreated. Healthy sessions (Claude running) still no-op. Edge cases: session not found → fresh create; pane_current_command error → treat as zombie. Test: go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/oro/ -run TestCreate_KillsZombie

title: Worktree manager should prune stale branches before creating
description: When a previous oro run fails mid-assignment, it can leave behind ghost worktrees (prunable) and stale agent/* branches. On the next run, git worktree add -b agent/<id> fails with 'branch already exists' (exit 255), causing an infinite retry loop of worktree_error events until the workers die. Fix: before running git worktree add, check if the branch exists and if the worktree dir is prunable. If so, run git worktree prune and git branch -D agent/<id> before retrying. This makes oro resilient to dirty restarts.

title: Add dispatcher-side message buffering for disconnected workers
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §3.6

**Problem:** Workers buffer messages during disconnect, but dispatcher has no buffering. ASSIGN/PREPARE_SHUTDOWN sent to disconnected worker is lost.

**Design:** Add pendingMsgs []protocol.Message to trackedWorker. sendToWorker() buffers up to 10 messages if worker disconnected. handleReconnect() replays pending messages. >10 pending = treat worker as dead.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go, pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: TestDispatcherBuffering | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: ASSIGN sent during disconnect delivered after reconnect; 11 pending messages = worker removed

title: Harden tmux escalation against shell injection
description:
**Spec ref:** docs/plans/2026-02-10-hardening-spec.md §2.4

**Problem:** sanitizeForTmux only strips \n and \r. Tmux send-keys interprets shell metacharacters. Attacker controlling QG output or bead titles could inject commands into manager pane.

**Design:** Option A (preferred): Replace send-keys with load-buffer + paste-buffer (treats content as literal). Option B: Aggressive sanitization removing backticks, $(), ;, &, |, <, >, etc.

**Files:** pkg/dispatcher/escalator.go, pkg/dispatcher/escalator_test.go

**Acceptance:**
- Test: pkg/dispatcher/escalator_test.go:TestEscalation_NoInjection | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... | Assert: message containing $(rm -rf /) rendered as literal text, not executed

**Problem:** beadID directly interpolated into filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".worktrees", beadID) and git branch "agent/" + beadID without validation. Crafted ID like ../../etc escapes directory.

**Design:** Add ValidateBeadID(id string) error to pkg/protocol. Regex: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}$. Call at all entry points: handleMessage, WorktreeManager.Create, assignBead.

**Problem:** Socket created with default umask. Any local user in same group can connect, send directives, impersonate workers.

**Design:** Define MaxMessageSize (1MB) in pkg/protocol. Configure scanner.Buffer() in both dispatcher handleConn and worker readMessages. Add ReconnectPayload.Validate() enforcing maxBufferedMessages on receive.

title: Codex ops MISSING_AC escalation should fail closed without scheduler loop

The failure did not resolve or quarantine the malformed bead, so the scheduler loop kept retrying and workers stayed idle.

Desired behavior:
When a MISSING_AC ops escalation fails under Codex, dispatcher should record the failure once, mark/quarantine the bead as non-assignable, and continue scheduling other executable work. The Codex ops adapter should also produce a useful error payload instead of opaque exit status when possible.

Read: pkg/dispatcher missing-AC escalation path, pkg/ops, pkg/agentruntime/codex, dispatcher event handling.
Edges: Claude runtime behavior remains unchanged; successful ops escalation still works; repeated failures are rate-limited or deduplicated so idle workers do not spin on the same bad bead.
Anti-pattern guard: do not paper over by disabling Codex runtime ops or by treating all ops failures as success. Failure must be visible and must not block unrelated scheduling.

title: oro init/setup installs canonical git hooks and prevents beads from re-injecting itself
description:
When `oro init` or `oro setup` runs in a target project, it should install the canonical git hooks (author identity guard, language-aware lint/format, quality gate on pre-push) and ensure beads cannot re-inject `BEADS INTEGRATION` blocks, `bd hook` shims, or any sync-on-commit logic into them.

Background:
- Today, oro maintains `.beads/` in the user's global gitignore (cmd_init.go:821) — good.
- But oro does NOT install/manage the git hooks themselves. The repo has `git/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push}` checked in + a `make install-git-hooks` target. In April 2026 this repo was hit by a regression where `bd hooks install` (or `bd` running as part of `bd update`) replaced 130+ lines of rich pre-commit content with a bare `exec bd hook pre-commit` shim (commit 4ea26aee → 8a40178f). Restored at 13c78417, regression-tested in scripts/test_git_hooks.sh AC5/AC6/AC7.
- We don't want to play whack-a-mole. `oro init`/`oro setup` should own the hooks and lock beads out.

Scope:
1. `oro init` (and/or `oro setup`) installs git hooks into the target project's `.git/hooks/` (not via symlink to a checked-in dir — write directly, since target projects won't have an oro hooks template).
2. Hooks are sourced from a canonical template embedded in the oro binary (likely under `cmd/oro/_assets/git-hooks/` alongside other embedded assets).
3. The hook content matches the rich design (ruff/gofumpt/golangci-lint/go test/shellcheck/biome/markdownlint/yamllint + author identity guard + pre-push quality gate). Language sections must skip cleanly when a language isn't present in the target repo.
4. Beads anti-injection: 
   a. After install, hooks contain a marker comment (e.g., `# managed by oro — do not allow bd hooks install to overwrite`).
   b. Document that users must NOT run `bd hooks install` in oro-managed repos.
   c. Optional: if feasible, set `bd` config (e.g., `.beads/config.yaml`) to disable bd's hook auto-management.
5. Idempotent: re-running `oro init`/`oro setup` is a no-op when hooks are already installed and match the template; warns + offers --force when they've drifted.
6. `oro uninstall` removes the installed hooks (cleanup parity with global gitignore cleanup at cmd_uninstall.go).

Out of scope:
- Per-language tooling install (assume ruff/gofumpt/etc. handle 'not installed' gracefully — they already do).
- Backporting to existing oro-managed projects automatically (one-time manual `oro setup --reinstall-hooks` is fine).
acceptance_criteria:
1. `oro init` in a fresh git repo writes `.git/hooks/pre-commit` and `.git/hooks/pre-push` matching the canonical template (verified by content hash or grep for design markers: 'Author identity guard', 'gofumpt', 'golangci-lint', 'quality_gate.sh').
2. Installed hooks are executable (mode 0755).
3. Hooks contain an oro-management marker comment that's clearly visible at the top of the file.
4. Re-running `oro init` on a repo with matching hooks is a no-op (no diff to .git/hooks/).
5. Re-running `oro init` on a repo with drifted hooks (e.g., bd-shim swap simulated by replacing pre-commit with `exec bd hook pre-commit`) prints a warning and refuses to overwrite without `--force`.
6. `oro uninstall` removes the installed hooks.
7. `bd` cannot silently rewrite the hooks: either via config that disables bd hook management OR via documentation + a runtime check in the hook itself that errors on `BEADS INTEGRATION` markers.
8. Existing scripts/test_git_hooks.sh AC5/AC6/AC7 pass against hooks installed by `oro init`.
9. Test coverage: a Go test that runs `oro init` against a tmp git repo and asserts hook content + permissions + idempotency + drift detection.
notes: test: verify auto-export disabled
close_reason: Implementation complete. Commit 5e552d51: installCanonicalHooks added to oro init/uninstall, idempotent install, drift detection with --force, HookDriftError type, bd-injection guard via marker comment, 16 Go tests covering all 9 ACs. Worker completed work but stalled before close; manager agent recovered.

title: Detect zombie-deferred beads on dispatcher startup
description:
Workaround for bd v1.0.2 bug: `bd update <id> --status=open` does not clear `defer_until`. Result: bead has status=open but defer_until still set; `bd ready` honors the timestamp and hides it from dispatcher; queue appears empty, workers idle. Encountered 2026-04-24 on scriptwriter-2jv (3-hour debug cost).

Memory: feedback_bd_zombie_defer_until.md (linked from MEMORY.md).

Implementation: in startup reconciliation (dispatcher.go:916 area, near startup_reconciliation_summary), enumerate all beads via `bd export`, find any with status=open AND defer_until set, log a 'zombie_deferred_detected' event per bead, and auto-fix each via the workaround cycle: `bd defer <id> --until=<far-future>` then `bd undefer <id>` (which actually nulls defer_until).

Upstream fix is preferable (filed separately) but this gives oro fast-path recovery so users don't lose hours debugging an empty queue.

title: fix(tmux): detect dead panes in SendKeysVerified and fail fast
description: SendKeysVerified retries send-keys for up to 60s against a dead pane (Claude crashed after showing prompt). tmux exposes #{pane_dead} format variable which returns '1' when the pane process has exited. Add isPaneDead(paneTarget) helper that queries this, and check it in the SendKeysVerified retry loop. On dead pane: capture last pane output and return immediately with actionable error like 'pane oro-X:architect is dead (exit N) — Claude may have crashed during startup. Last output: ...'.
acceptance_criteria: 1. SendKeysVerified returns immediately (no 60s wait) when pane is dead, with error containing 'dead' and last pane output. 2. SendKeysVerified retries normally when pane is alive but send-keys fails transiently. 3. isPaneDead returns false (fail-open) when display-message itself errors. 4. go test ./cmd/oro/... passes.

title: fix(init): generate quality_gate.sh even when no languages detected
description: writeQualityGateScriptFile (quality_gate_gen.go:395-397) early-returns when cfg has zero languages, preventing generation of even a shell-only quality gate. The downstream renderer writeQualityGateScript handles zero languages fine (HasGo=false, HasPython=false). This causes oro start to warn 'quality_gate.sh is missing' after oro setup on projects without detected languages. Fix: remove the len(cfg.Languages)==0 guard so the renderer runs unconditionally when a config file exists.
acceptance_criteria: 1. writeQualityGateScriptFile produces a file when config.yaml exists but has zero languages. 2. writeQualityGateScriptFile still skips (no error) when config.yaml is truly absent. 3. Generated shell-only script passes bash -n syntax check. 4. go test ./cmd/oro/... passes.

title: Harden worktree Create(): return pruneStale errors and log worktree_create_prune_failed event
description:
pruneStale() silently ignores all git step errors (worktree remove, prune, branch -D). When git branch -D fails, the Create() retry also fails, worktreeFailures cooldown fires, but the log only shows a generic worktree_error with the retry's git message — not which pruneStale step failed.

Fix:
1. Change pruneStale() signature to return error, capturing and returning the first non-nil git step error
2. In Create(), if pruneStale() returns an error, log a worktree_create_prune_failed dispatcher event with the step error before attempting the retry
3. The retry still runs (don't skip it — git branch -D failure is rare but the retry might still work if branch was eventually freed)
4. If the retry also fails, the existing worktree_error event + cooldown path handles it

Files to change: pkg/dispatcher/worktree_manager.go, pkg/dispatcher/worktree_manager_test.go
acceptance_criteria:

title: Add oro attach command to connect to running tmux session
description:
## Summary
Add `oro attach` CLI command that connects to a running oro tmux session.
Currently users must know `tmux attach -t oro` — the CLI should provide this.

## Design spec
docs/plans/2026-02-26-oro-attach-design.md

## Files to create
- `cmd/oro/cmd_attach.go` — new command implementation
- `cmd/oro/cmd_attach_test.go` — tests

## Files to modify
- `cmd/oro/root.go` — add `newAttachCmd()` to `cmd.AddCommand(...)` in `newRootCmd()`
- `cmd/oro/cmd_help.go` — add "attach" line after "start" in hardcoded `helpText` const

## Behavior matrix
| Daemon | Tmux | Healthy? | TTY? | Behavior |
|--------|------|----------|------|----------|
| Running | Exists | Yes | Yes | Attach (select architect window first) |
| Running | Exists | No | Yes | Error: "session unhealthy — run oro stop && oro start" |
| Running | Exists | Yes | No | Error: "cannot attach without a terminal" |
| Running | Missing | — | — | Error: "dispatcher running in daemon-only mode" |
| Stopped | — | — | — | Error: "no running session — use oro start" |
| Stale | — | — | — | Error: "stale PID found — run oro cleanup then oro start" |

## Key implementation notes
- TTY check MUST use `isatty.IsTerminal(os.Stdin.Fd())` — NOT Stdout
- Reuse existing: DaemonStatus(), TmuxSession.Exists(), isHealthy(), AttachInteractive()
- isHealthy() is unexported but same package (cmd/oro is package main), so accessible
- Session name from TmuxSession.Name field, not hardcoded "oro" string literal

## Acceptance criteria
1. `oro attach` connects to a running healthy tmux session
2. `oro attach` errors with actionable messages for all 5 error cases in behavior matrix
3. `oro help` shows `attach` in the Lifecycle section between start and stop
4. No behavior change to `oro start`

## Tests (7)
- TestAttachNoSession: daemon stopped → error with "use oro start"
- TestAttachStale: stale PID → error with "oro cleanup"
- TestAttachDaemonOnly: daemon running, no tmux → error with "daemon-only mode"
- TestAttachUnhealthy: tmux exists but unhealthy → error with "oro stop && oro start"
- TestAttachNoTTY: tmux exists + healthy but no TTY → error
- TestAttachSuccess: tmux exists + healthy + TTY → calls AttachInteractive
- TestHelpShowsAttach: oro help output contains "attach" in Lifecycle section

Signature: func newAttachCmd() *cobra.Command

title: Fix idle worker reconnect sends empty BeadID causing spurious rejections
description:
When an idle worker reconnects after a network glitch, it sends MsgReconnect with BeadID='' (empty string). The dispatcher's validateReconnectBead() tries to look up bead '' which always fails, logging reconnect_closed_bead_rejected. The worker should re-register as idle cleanly without going through bead validation.

Root cause: pkg/worker/worker.go reconnect logic always sends a Reconnect message with whatever beadID is set (empty for idle workers).

Fix: In the dispatcher's reconnect handler (dispatcher.go), if BeadID is empty, skip bead validation and transition worker directly to idle state.

title: Add log file output to oro work (reuse worker log infrastructure)
description:
Make oro work write Claude output to the same log file infrastructure that dispatcher workers use, so oro logs works for both.

## Problem
When oro work runs in background, there's no way to see what Claude is doing. Only logStep() calls to stderr (5-6 lines total). Claude stdout is piped through DrainOutput() to stderr but lost when backgrounded. Dispatcher workers already have per-worker log files at ~/.oro/workers/<id>/output.log with oro logs --raw --follow.

## Goal
oro work writes Claude output to ~/.oro/workers/work-<bead-id>/output.log. oro logs work-<bead-id> --raw --follow works immediately with zero changes to cmd_logs.go.

## Spec
Full design: docs/plans/2026-02-24-oro-work-observability-design.md

## Files to Change
- cmd/oro/cmd_work.go: Open log file in executeWork(), pass handle to spawnAndWait(). Add logOut package var (io.Writer), set to io.MultiWriter(os.Stderr, logFile) when logFile non-nil. Write attempt separators and phase markers via logOut instead of hardcoded os.Stderr.
- pkg/worker/drain.go: Change DrainOutput echo param from io.Writer to ...io.Writer (variadic). Filter nil writers, use io.MultiWriter internally. Backwards compatible — existing single-writer callers unchanged.
- pkg/worker/drain_test.go: Add test for multi-writer fan-out.
- cmd/oro/cmd_work_test.go: Add test that log file is created and contains output.

## Key Details
- Log dir: ~/.oro/workers/work-<bead-id>/ (prefix distinguishes from dispatcher worker-<timestamp>-<n>)
- Multiple attempts append to same log with --- attempt N (model) --- separator lines
- logStep() writes to logOut package var (not hardcoded os.Stderr)
- Log persists after exit; dispatcher wipes ~/.oro/workers/ on startup = free cleanup
- oro logs doesn't validate worker ID format; works with work-* IDs immediately (verify in cmd_logs.go first)
acceptance_criteria:
1. oro work <bead-id> writes Claude output to ~/.oro/workers/work-<bead-id>/output.log
2. oro logs work-<bead-id> --raw displays the log content without changes to cmd_logs.go
3. Multiple attempts are separated by --- attempt N (model) --- markers in the log
4. DrainOutput variadic change doesn't break existing callers
5. go test ./cmd/oro/... ./pkg/worker/... passes
notes: Spec file: docs/plans/2026-02-24-oro-work-observability-design.md

title: test(dispatcher): kill bead_tracker.go mutation survivors
description: 35 of 46 bead_tracker.go mutants survived go-mutesting (24% kill rate). Add targeted tests to kill the survivors.
acceptance_criteria: Test: pkg/dispatcher/tracking_leak_test.go | Cmd: go test ./pkg/dispatcher/... -count=1 -race | Assert: go-mutesting kill rate for bead_tracker.go >= 70%
notes:
## Surviving mutant categories

### 1. Individual map deletes in clearBeadTracking (9 mutants) — EASY
One mutant per tracked map: attemptCounts, handoffCounts, rejectionCounts, pendingHandoffs,
qgStuckTracker, escalatedBeads, worktreeFailures, exhaustedBeads, assigningBeads.
Tests check that *something* is cleared but not that *each specific map* is emptied.
Fix: after clearBeadTracking(beadID), assert each map[beadID] is gone.

### 2. Individual map deletes in deleteOrphanedTracking (9 mutants) — EASY
Same 9 maps, same issue — deletions inside the orphan pruning loop are not individually verified.
Fix: populate each map with a beadID, call deleteOrphanedTracking with no active beads,
assert each map entry is removed.

### 3. Lock/Unlock no-ops (10 mutants) — LOW ROI
d.mu.Lock() and d.mu.Unlock() removed from clearBeadTracking, clearRejectionCount,
clearHandoffCount, consumePendingHandoff. Tests never exercise concurrent access.
These require -race flag + concurrent goroutines to catch. Skip for now unless
the race detector already exercises these paths.

### 4. activeBeads set population (2 mutants) — MEDIUM

title: Document or persist embedder vocab across restarts
description:
NewEmbedder() creates empty vocab. After dispatcher restart, existing DB embeddings use dimension indices from the old vocab but new queries use fresh indices. CosineSimilarity between mismatched vocabs produces noise. HybridSearch degrades silently to FTS5-only via RRF.

Options:
A) Persist vocab to DB (serialize map on shutdown, load on startup) — full fix
B) Re-embed all memories on startup from stored text — expensive but correct
C) Accept degradation, document it, ensure FTS5 weight dominates RRF — cheapest

title: Update dispatching-parallel-agents skill: pipeline mode + oro workers
description:
Upgrade the dispatching-parallel-agents skill with these changes:

1. **Pipeline mode as default**: Merge-as-you-go instead of batch. Each completed worker is immediately merged and the next bead launched from the queue, keeping N workers saturated.

2. **Default to oro workers**: Use `oro work <bead-id>` as primary dispatch method (handles worktree, TDD, QG, ops review, merge). Raw Task agents become fallback.

3. **FF-merge with active worktrees**: Document that when workers are still running, you can't rebase (guard hook blocks). Use ff-merge when branch shares same base, cherry-pick when it diverges. No need to kill active workers.

4. **Dependency-aware scheduling**: Same file = sequential deps, different files = parallel. Document the pattern we used for dispatcher_test.go (7in4.4.1→.2→.3 sequential, 7in4.4.4-.7 parallel).

5. **Resource concurrency limits**: Default to 5 oro workers. Task agents can go higher (lighter weight). Document that resource contention (signal:killed) was observed at 2 concurrent claude processes in earlier sessions, but 5 is the target.

6. **Stale worktree preflight**: Check for orphaned worktrees from previous sessions at start. `git worktree list` and clean up.

7. **Error/retry strategy**: When a worker fails — inspect worktree state, fix and recommit manually, or re-dispatch. Don't blindly retry.

8. **bd file contention**: Multiple workers closing beads modify .beads/issues.jsonl. Note this as a known merge friction point — merge order doesn't matter for this file, just take latest.

Files: .claude/skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md, assets/skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md
acceptance_criteria: Test: manual review | Cmd: diff .claude/skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md assets/skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md | Assert: Files match. Skill describes pipeline as default pattern. oro work is primary dispatch method. Raw Task agents documented as fallback. Merge-as-you-go replaces batch merge section.
notes: 9. **Claim bead in worker prompt**: Worker template must include `bd update <id> --status=in_progress` at start, not just `bd close` at end. Without this, active work is invisible to `bd list --status=in_progress`.

title: Dispatcher-spawned workers log to daemon log instead of per-worker files
description:
ExecProcessManager.Spawn (pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:88-89) sets cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout and cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr. When the dispatcher runs as a daemon, os.Stdout and os.Stderr are the daemon's log file (/tmp/oro-daemon.log), so all worker output (including claude -p stdout and stderr) gets mixed into the daemon log. Individual worker log files (~/.oro/workers/<id>/output.log) are never created for dispatcher-managed workers. This makes per-worker debugging impossible via oro logs or by inspecting worker log dirs.

Contrast with ExecWorkerSpawner.SpawnWorker (cmd/oro/cmd_worker_launch.go:28-52) which properly creates per-worker log files and redirects child stdout/stderr there.

Observed: ran oro start --detach with 3 workers. ls ~/.oro/workers/ | grep worker-177 showed only one worker-1771377396051711000-1 dir (the one launched via oro worker launch path), and its log was empty. Workers 0 and 2 had no log dirs at all because they were spawned by the dispatcher's reconcileScale -> ExecProcessManager.Spawn path.

Fix: Add oroHome string field to ExecProcessManager. In NewOroProcessManager, accept oroHome as parameter. In Spawn(id), create log dir at filepath.Join(oroHome, 'workers', id) via os.MkdirAll, open output.log (O_CREATE|O_WRONLY|O_APPEND), set cmd.Stdout = logFile and cmd.Stderr = logFile. Close parent copy of logFile after cmd.Start(). Thread oroHome through the call site in cmd/oro/cmd_start.go where NewOroProcessManager is called.

Read: pkg/dispatcher/process_manager.go:ExecProcessManager.Spawn (lines 86-110), cmd/oro/cmd_worker_launch.go:ExecWorkerSpawner.SpawnWorker (lines 28-52), cmd/oro/cmd_start.go (search for NewOroProcessManager call site)

Signature: func NewOroProcessManager(socketPath, oroHome string) *ExecProcessManager

Edges:
- oroHome empty string -> fall back to os.Stdout/os.Stderr with a logged warning (don't silently swallow output)
- log directory creation fails -> return error from Spawn (don't silently drop logs)
- log file open fails -> return error from Spawn
- parent closes its logFile fd after Start() -> child process still has the fd open (standard Go pattern, matches ExecWorkerSpawner)

title: Use live queue depth in status response instead of stale cache
description:
## Problem
`oro status` shows a stale queue depth. The dispatcher uses `d.cachedQueueDepth` (dispatcher.go:1930) in `buildStatusJSON()`, which is only updated when `tryAssign()` runs on the polling interval (dispatcher.go:1562-1564). Between poll ticks, the status response shows outdated data.

## Root Cause
`buildStatusJSON()` reads `d.cachedQueueDepth` under lock, but this value was set the last time `tryAssign()` ran. The status directive is user-triggered (via `oro status`), so it can happen at any time between assign loop ticks.

## Fix
In `buildStatusJSON()`, call `d.beads.Ready(ctx)` to get a live bead count instead of using `d.cachedQueueDepth`. Since status is user-triggered and infrequent, the extra bead source call is acceptable latency.

Note: `buildStatusJSON()` currently takes no context parameter — its signature is `func (d *Dispatcher) buildStatusJSON() string`. It will need `ctx context.Context` added (and the call site at dispatcher.go:1830 updated to pass `ctx`).

## Files
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1911 — `buildStatusJSON()`: add ctx param, call `d.beads.Ready(ctx)`
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1830 — call site: pass ctx
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:1930 — replace `d.cachedQueueDepth` with live count
- pkg/dispatcher/dispatcher_test.go — update tests for new signature

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: `buildStatusJSON` returns current bead count from bead source, not stale cached value
- [ ] Test: status response `queue_depth` matches actual `beads.Ready()` count at time of request
- [ ] Existing status tests still pass

title: Simplify session close protocol: remove redundant bd sync calls
description:
## Context

The session close protocol in multiple files calls `bd sync` twice, but the
pre-commit git hook (`.git/hooks/pre-commit`) already runs `bd sync --flush-only`
and `git add .beads/issues.jsonl` on every commit. The manual syncs are redundant.

### Evidence

- `.git/hooks/pre-commit`: runs `bd sync --flush-only` then `git add .beads/issues.jsonl`
- `.git/hooks/post-merge`: runs `bd import -i .beads/issues.jsonl` after pull
- `bd sync` (no flags) only exports DB→JSONL, does NOT stage/commit
- The only case where manual sync matters: beads changes with no subsequent commit

## Change

Replace the current 6-step protocol:
```
[ ] 1. git status
[ ] 2. git add <files>
[ ] 3. bd sync              ← redundant
[ ] 4. git commit -m "..."
[ ] 5. bd sync              ← redundant
[ ] 6. git push
```

With the simplified protocol:
```
[ ] 1. bd close <ids>          (finish beads work)
[ ] 2. git add <files>         (stage code changes)
[ ] 3. git commit -m "..."     (pre-commit hook auto-syncs beads)
[ ] 4. git push
```

## Files to update

1. `~/.claude/rules/beads.md` — "Landing the Plane" section
   - Remove explicit `bd sync` step
   - Add note that pre-commit hook handles beads export automatically
   - Simplify the checklist

2. `~/.oro/panes/architect/handoff.yaml` — SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL section
   - Same simplification

3. Search for any other files referencing the double-sync pattern:
   - `grep -r "bd sync" ~/.claude/ ~/.oro/` and update as needed

## Acceptance criteria
1. No file in ~/.claude/rules/ or ~/.oro/ references the double bd sync pattern
2. Session close protocol is 4 steps (close, add, commit, push) not 6
3. A note exists explaining that the pre-commit hook auto-syncs beads
acceptance_criteria: 1. No file in ~/.claude/rules/ or ~/.oro/ references the double bd sync pattern; 2. Session close protocol is 4 steps (close, add, commit, push) not 6; 3. A note exists explaining that the pre-commit hook auto-syncs beads

title: Add step-by-step startup log with spinner to oro start
description:
## Context

`oro start` takes 60-120 seconds with ZERO user feedback until the final
'oro swarm started' line. Add a step-by-step log that prints each phase
as it completes, with an animated spinner during long waits.

## Target output

```
✓ Preflight checks passed
✓ Daemon started (PID 1234)
✓ Dispatcher socket ready
⠋ Waiting for architect...        ← spinner animates during ~30-45s wait
✓ Architect ready (34s)
⠋ Waiting for manager...
✓ Manager ready (31s)
✓ Beacon verified
oro swarm started (PID 1234, workers=2, model=sonnet)
```

## Implementation

### 1. Add a startup logger helper in cmd/oro/startup_log.go

Create a small `startupLog` struct with methods:
- `Step(msg string)` — prints `✓ <msg>` with green checkmark
- `StepTimed(msg string, d time.Duration)` — prints `✓ <msg> (Xs)` 
- `StartSpinner(msg string) func()` — starts goroutine printing braille spinner
  `⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏` at ~80ms interval on same line via `\r`. Returns a stop func
  that kills spinner and prints the final `✓` line.
- Non-TTY fallback: check `isatty.IsTerminal(os.Stdout.Fd())` — if false, just
  print static lines without spinner animation. `go-isatty` already imported.
- Use `context.Context` for cancellation — stop func cancels spinner goroutine.

### 2. Wire into cmd/oro/cmd_start.go

In `runFullStart()` (line ~98):

```go
log := newStartupLog(os.Stdout)
```

Insert calls at each phase boundary:
- After `preflightAndCheckRunning()` returns: `log.Step("Preflight checks passed")`
- After `SpawnDaemon()` returns: `log.Step(fmt.Sprintf("Daemon started (PID %d)", pid))`
- Before socket poll loop (line 113): `stop := log.StartSpinner("Waiting for dispatcher socket...")`
- After socket ready: `stop()` then `log.Step("Dispatcher socket ready")`
- Inside `TmuxSession.Create()` — needs a callback or logger interface passed in:
  - Before each `WaitForPrompt`: `stop := log.StartSpinner(fmt.Sprintf("Waiting for %s...", role))`
  - After prompt ready: `stop()` then `log.StepTimed(fmt.Sprintf("%s ready", role), elapsed)`
  - Before `VerifyBeaconReceived`: `stop := log.StartSpinner("Verifying beacon...")`
  - After beacon verified: `stop()` then `log.Step("Beacon verified")`
- Keep existing final line: `"oro swarm started (PID %d, workers=%d, model=%s)\n"`

### 3. Pass logger into TmuxSession.Create

`TmuxSession.Create()` in `tmux.go:200` is where the long waits happen. Either:
- Add a `Logger` field to `TmuxSession` struct, or
- Add a `StartupLogger` parameter to `Create()`
- The logger interface: `type StartupLogger interface { Step(string); StepTimed(string, time.Duration); StartSpinner(string) func() }`

### Key files
- `cmd/oro/cmd_start.go` — runFullStart() orchestrator (line ~98-147)
- `cmd/oro/tmux.go` — TmuxSession.Create() (line ~200), WaitForPrompt, SendKeysVerified
- `cmd/oro/startup_log.go` — NEW file for startupLog helper
- `cmd/oro/startup_log_test.go` — NEW file for tests

### Non-TTY handling
`go-isatty` is already imported in cmd_start.go. When stdout is not a TTY:
- Skip spinner animation entirely
- Print static lines: "Waiting for architect..." then "✓ Architect ready (34s)"

## Acceptance criteria
1. `oro start` prints step-by-step progress including ✓ checkmarks for completed phases
2. Long-wait phases (pane readiness) show an animated braille spinner that updates in-place
3. Non-TTY output (piped) degrades gracefully to static lines without ANSI escape codes
4. No spinner goroutine leaks — all spinners cleaned up on error paths and normal completion

title: CLI status formatting with alerts, -v/--full/--json flags
description:
## Problem
CLI oro status currently shows 5 bare lines. Design calls for tiered output with alerts-first formatting and multiple verbosity levels.

## Design
Consume enriched statusResponse from dispatcher (oro-vii8.1) and format into sections.

### Flags
- (default): alerts + summary + active beads with health
- `-v`: + worker health table, QG/retry counters per bead, uptime, config, pending handoffs
- `--full`: + bd ready/blocked/in-progress lists (shells out to bd)
- `--json`: JSON output at selected tier level

### Alerts Section (top, only when problems exist)
Computed CLI-side from enriched data:
- Workers with no progress > ProgressTimeout/2 → warning; > ProgressTimeout → critical
- Beads with attemptCounts >= 2 → QG failure alert
- Pending handoffs > 0 → handoff alert

### Default Output Format
```
ALERTS:
  ⚠ worker-3: no progress (12min)
  ✗ oro-xyz: QG failed 3x

dispatcher: running (PID 1234)
  state:   running
  workers: 3 active, 2 idle (target: 5)
  focus:   epic-42
  queue:   5 ready

active beads:
  worker-1 → oro-abc (healthy, 2m ago)
  worker-2 → oro-def (healthy, 30s ago)
```

## Files
- cmd/oro/cmd_status.go — expand statusResponse, add flags, formatStatusResponse sections, alert computation
- cmd/oro/cmd_status_test.go — test formatting, flags, alerts

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: cmd/oro/cmd_status_test.go:TestFormatStatusResponse_DefaultWithAlerts | Cmd: go test -race ./cmd/oro/... -run TestFormatStatusResponse_DefaultWithAlerts | Assert: output contains ALERTS section with stuck worker warning when lastProgress exceeds half of ProgressTimeout, and shows worker summary with active/idle/target counts
- [ ] Test: cmd/oro/cmd_status_test.go:TestFormatStatusResponse_JSONFlag | Cmd: go test -race ./cmd/oro/... -run TestFormatStatusResponse_JSONFlag | Assert: --json flag produces valid JSON matching enriched statusResponse struct
- [ ] Test: cmd/oro/cmd_status_test.go:TestFormatStatusResponse_VerboseFlag | Cmd: go test -race ./cmd/oro/... -run TestFormatStatusResponse_VerboseFlag | Assert: -v flag includes worker health table and attempt counts per bead
